Some default shortcuts don't work with non-english layout: `cmd + .`, etc
body:
## The What

VSCode should use keywords for hotkey (like `[Period]`), rather than pure symbols (like `.`), - for the default key settings that have <kbd>cmd</kbd> or <kbd>ctrl</kbd> in it.

## The Why

So default shortcuts could work universally between all the layouts, so no one has to manually fix those default settings for this purpose.

For example:

- In English layout "Quick Action" shortcut counts as: <kbd>cmd + .</kbd>, since `.` is `.`
- In Russian layout "Quick Action" shortcut counts as: <kbd>cmd + ю</kbd>, but pure symbols (`.`) don’t count this: `ю` isn't `.`
- But if it were <kbd>cmd + [Period]</kbd> in setttings, not <kbd>cmd + .</kbd>, then it would both count as <kbd>cmd + .</kbd> and <kbd>cmd + ю</kbd>, - because they're both the same physical key, - which is neat! (Thanks VSCode for having those keywords)

Therefore the default "Quick Fix" action does not work sometimes when you're using other than English layout, so user has to change the layout, which is… Irritating.

Alternatively, user has to fix default hotkeys in settings himself, changing those `.` to `[Period]` manually… Which is unfortunate.

## The How

TL;DR: Change the default shortcuts so they use the mentioned keywords (like `[Period]`), instead of pure signs (like `.`).

As I said, a user can solve each problematic hornet with custom setting like in this example:

```jsonc
// ✅ Good: English layout is respected in whatever currently chosen language in OS
{
  "key": "cmd+[Period]",
  "command": "editor.action.quickFix",
  "when": "editorHasCodeActionsProvider && editorTextFocus && !editorReadonly"
}
```

This `[Period]` keyword makes it work throughout different layouts, as long as it shares the same physical key with whatever else symbols in other than English language. But the defaults, it seems, uses the pure symbols:

```jsonc
// ❌ Bad: Although this hotkey works in English layout, however in Russian layout the same (physically) key doesn’t output a dot symbol, thus it doesn’t fire the «Quick Fix» action
{
  "key": "cmd+.",
  "command": "editor.action.quickFix",
  "when": "editorHasCodeActionsProvider && editorTextFocus && !editorReadonly"
}
```

So hence the problem: VSCode default shortcuts don't work with non-english layout sometimes. This fix (the keywords) should be used throughout all the default keys, in order to solve the issue.

## Other problematic shortcuts (examples):

Although I don't know all the concrete examples, there are few ones that I stumbled upon, other than <kbd>shift + cmd + .</kbd>:

- <kbd>cmd + shift + {</kbd> (`shift+cmd+х` in Russian layout)
- <kbd>cmd + shift + }</kbd> (`shift+cmd+ъ` in russian layout)

title: [json] Add support for extensions associating JSON schemas with documents dynamically (via API)
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

Add support for extensions associating JSON schemas with documents dynamically (via API).

Right now, it is only possible to associate a JSON schema with a text document by:

1. using schemas directly built-in into VSCode, e.g., `package.json`, `.babelrc` , ...

2. explicitly [mapping it in the user settings](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/json#_mapping-in-the-user-settings)

3. explicitly [mapping it in the workspace](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/json#_mapping-to-a-schema-in-the-workspace)

4. explicitly [mapping it in an extension via a file-match pattern](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/json#_file-match-syntax)

But all these associations are static and working only on a folder path and filename matching.

I would like to be able to dynamically/programmatically associate a JSON schema with a document within an extension.

E.g., the extension could first inspect the content of the file and check for specific well-known conditions in order to decide, which JSON schema (or if at all) should be associated with a given text document.

E.g., within our organization we have a lot of different file formats with existing JSON schemas, but we don't have canonical/standardized folders and filenames for the files that would need validation against these JSON schemas, with most of them just ending on `*.json` somewhere in the folder tree.

I could imagine a mechanism like this to associate a JSON schema with a JSON document `doc`:

```
registerJsonSchema(doc, schemaId, schemaSrc)
```

with a unique `schemaId` provided by the extension and `schemaSrc` either be `URL` or a local file reference.

If the same `schemaId` is provided for a `doc` with no `schemaSrc` the JSON schema association is removed again from that document.

Theoretically `schemaSrc` could also be a JSON schema object (similar to a [schema directly defined in the settings](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/json#_mapping-to-a-schema-defined-in-settings)), which would allow you to dynamically build up a schema by the extension and provide this for validation.

And since a lot of configuration files are not just `JSON` files but also `YAML` files, some bonus points for allowing the association of JSON schemas also to `YAML` files, not just `JSON` files.

Note, that there is also another related feature request: `Support for contentMatch in addition to fileMatch for extension contributes.jsonValidation` https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/229696

title: [macOS] Custom terminal not found on first launch
body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.93.1 - OS Version: macOS Sonoma 14.5 We're using a custom terminal (provided by our extension) set as the default terminal in a .code-workspace. When launching VS Code, the wrong terminal is being used for the first terminal instance created. Every subsequent terminal is created using our custom terminal as expected. This can lead to issues when using our extension because we are providing environment variables to the terminal that are missing when the wrong terminal is used. I've tried adjusting the extension activation settings and confirmed that the extension is indeed activating. I am able to reproduce the same issue using the terminal-sample in the VS Code extension samples repo, so it doesn't appear to be specific to our extension. I can only reproduce this issue on macOS - I could not reproduce on Windows 10. Steps to Reproduce: 1. Clone the `terminal-sample` (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-extension-samples/tree/main/terminal-sample). 2. Build and debug the sample. 3. Close the Terminal view, if open. 4. Create a workspace (`File > Save Workspace As...`) and save it anywhere. 5. In the workspace settings, set the custom terminal as the default: ``` "settings": { "terminal.integrated.defaultProfile.osx": "Terminal API Profile", } ``` 6. Reload the debugged VS Code Window using the Command Palette (`Developer: Reload Window`) 7. Open the workspace settings and note the warning under the "Terminal API Profile": 8. Create a new terminal. This should use the "Terminal API Profile" by default, but it opens `zsh` instead. 9. Create another new terminal. The "Terminal API Profile" is correctly used.

- VS Code Version: 1.93.1
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise Version 24H2 (OS Build 26100.1742)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install Python and Pylance extensions
2. Open a notebook or create a notebook file with the following content, and press `ctrl + i` to open the copilot inline chat
```python
# notebook1.ipynb
def foo():
    print("foo")
```
3. Ask for a code change, then run inlineChat.viewInChat on the response (ctrl+down)![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b966f00a-773a-4307-a262-c964c2babba6)
4. Pylance crashes with bad request
```
2024-09-30 14:25:21.458 [info] [Error - 2:25:21 PM] Request textDocument/documentSymbol failed.
2024-09-30 14:25:21.458 [info]   Message: Request textDocument/documentSymbol failed with message: Debug Failure. Notebook file should not be passed to getWorkspaceForFile: vscode-chat-code-block:/c%3A/Users/stellahuang/source/projects/issue6427/notebook1.ipynb?6ff16a3c-1351-4aff-837f-d29e7cb883a7
  Code: -32603
```

When inspecting the [textDocument/documentSymbol](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#textDocument_documentSymbol) request from the Pylance side, I noticed that the `DocumentSymbolParams.textDocument.uri = 'vscode-chat-code-block:/c%3A/Users/stellahuang/source/projects/issue6427/notebook1.ipynb?3574a4e6-6692-4217-86b1-0ca8750d25f6'`. It looks like the query is for the notebook file itself, not for a specific cell, which seems like a bug.

Related bug opened in Pylance: https://github.com/microsoft/pylance-release/issues/6454

title: `chat.agentFilesLocations`, `chat.promptFilesLocations`, and `chat.agentSkillsLocations` resolve custom paths on remote host instead of local host during Remote SSH sessions
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.37.1
- VS Code Version: 1.109
- OS Version: Windows 11 (local) → Remote SSH to Ubuntu Linux
- Feature: Agent mode — custom agents, prompts, and skills discovery via Remote SSH
- Selected model: N/A
- Logs: Diagnostics output included below

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On the LOCAL machine, configure User settings:
   ```json
   "chat.agentFilesLocations": {
       "~/.copilot/myagent/agents": true
   },
   "chat.promptFilesLocations": {
       "~/.copilot/myagent/prompts": true
   },
   "chat.agentSkillsLocations": {
       "~/.copilot/myagent/skills": true
   }
   ```
2. Place valid `.agent.md`, `.prompt.md`, and skill files in those
   directories on the LOCAL machine. Confirm they exist locally.
3. Open a LOCAL VS Code window (no remote) — agents, prompts, and skills
   ARE discovered correctly. ✅
4. Connect to a remote machine via Remote SSH.
5. Open Chat Diagnostics (right-click Chat view → Diagnostics).
6. All three custom paths show: ❌ "Folder does not exist" ❌
   The paths exist on the local machine but are not found.
7. Place the same files at the same paths on the REMOTE machine.
   The files ARE now discovered. ✅
   However, this is not the expected behavior — these are User settings
   with files on the local machine.

Expected: Paths in `chat.agentFilesLocations`, `chat.promptFilesLocations`,
and `chat.agentSkillsLocations` should resolve on the LOCAL machine during
Remote SSH sessions, since these are User settings and the files exist
locally. The built-in "User Data" path (`%APPDATA%/Code/User/prompts/`)
correctly resolves on the local machine in remote sessions — custom
location paths should behave the same way.

Actual: Custom paths are resolved on the REMOTE host instead of the local
host. The `~` expands to the remote user's home directory, not the local
user's home directory. This forces users to duplicate files onto every
remote machine, defeating the purpose of User-level settings.

Diagnostics output (during Remote SSH session):

  Custom Agents — 2 files loaded
  ❌ ~/.copilot/myagent/agents - Folder does not exist
  ❌ %userprofile%/.copilot/myagent/agents - Folder does not exist
  User Data ← (this works, resolves locally)
  └─ test-in-prompts-dir.agent.md (from %APPDATA%/Code/User/prompts/)

  Prompt Files — 5 files loaded
  ❌ ~/.copilot/myagent/prompts - Folder does not exist
  User Data ← (this works, resolves locally)

  Skills
  ❌ ~/.copilot/myagent/skills - Folder does not exist

Workaround for agents and prompts: Place `.agent.md` and `.prompt.md` files
in `%APPDATA%/Code/User/prompts/` on the local machine — the built-in
"User Data" path resolves locally even during remote sessions.

Workaround for skills: Must duplicate skill files onto every remote machine
at the configured path (e.g. `~/.copilot/myagent/skills/`). There is no
way to have skills load from the local machine during Remote SSH sessions.

This may be related to PR #289275 which updated path resolution in
promptFilesLocator.ts. The custom location paths appear to be completely
non-functional during Remote SSH sessions, unlike the built-in "User Data"
path which correctly resolves locally.

body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No Yes - VS Code Version: 1.109.2 - OS Version: WIndows 11 Pro 25H2 (26200.7623) - WSL version: 2.6.3.0 - WSL kernel version: 6.6.87.2-1 - Machine: laptop with AMD Ryzen HX 370 32GB Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open vscode window in WSL2 2. Hibernate PC for a long time (>3h) 3. Powerup PC 4. See error window "Cannot reconnect. Please reload the window" 5. Click "Reload Window" button 6. Work normally 7. Cycle from point 2 In general I have problem with vscode on wsl after hibernation. It works normally in usual operations, it works normally after hibernete for a small time period like 15 minutes or 2 hours, but after long hibernate (longer than 3 hours) after waking up i see the error window: After reloading it works again, but it's annoying to reload it everyday after hibernation, especially whet you work with multiple windows. In dev console after waking up I see this: Here we can see that there is some timeout of 10800s that is equal to 3 hours. I suspect that this is happening because some modern timesync mechanisms (it did not happen on my old laptop with win10): after waking up machine is syncing time immediately, vscode checks last "ping" from server and current time, sees more then 3h gap and resets connection. I tried: 1. check time on windows and wsl after hiberation and it is correct 2. another windows installation on this machine 3. reinstall vscode 4. reinstall wsl distributive 5. quit docker for desktop 6. remove vscode server folder from home directory in wsl Nothing helped In meantime: 1. it worked OK on my old laptop with windows 10 and Ryzen 4700U 2. It works OK on my VMWare virtual machine (but instead of windows hibernation hypervisor's suspend mechanism used) Also issue persists trough several vscode updates, I can't tell where it started, I just saw this after moving to the new laptop a couple months ago.

title: Feature Request [copilot-chat]: Add some suggested quick responses.
body: It would be a great idea to add a couple of suggested quick 1 or 2 worded responses to send in the chat. Examples of when to apply the quick suggestions: - When Copilot suggests a list of changes to make, but doesn't make the changes itself due to the user only wanting reasons to change or suggestions. - When Copilot asks if we want it to make the changes. The quick suggestions would just be generic, like: - Yes / Yes please - No / No thanks - Apply change(s) And these suggestions could appear underneath the last Copilot message and would be dismissible. So clicking a suggested response would automatically send it into chat and the suggestions would disappear so that it doesn't clutter the chat as a persisted message. Could also potentially open this up to a new user setting to add/remove suggested responses.

title: Expose more Copilot Chat APIs for third-party model providers
body:
I recently developed a [VS Code extension](https://github.com/selfagency/opilot) that integrates an Ollama provider into GitHub Copilot Chat that is significantly more feature-rich than the default BYOK provider.

In the process, I came to conclude that it would be quite helpful to third-party model providers if the Copilot extension would expose more of the APIs Copilot uses with its own models.

For example, I had to write [my own stream parser](https://github.com/selfagency/llm-stream-parser) that could handle `thinking` and tool calling because the Copilot Chat extension doesn't expose its own. I also had to create my own settings panel for tweaking model settings (reasoning level, context window, etc.) because I can't currently access the APIs that GitHub models can.

Please consider making it easier for other model providers to integrate with Copilot chat.

title: .mcp.json from plugins doesn't work with environment variables templates
body:
When creating plugins with MCP servers setup inside the plugin, the environment variables are not replaced inside the `.mcp.json`, causing the variable template to be passed to the service as is, instead of causing the substitution. (This is not an issue when the MCP is set at the user level `mcp.json`)

- VS Code Version: 1.113.0
- OS Version: Mac OS Sequoia

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create a plugin containing an mcp server (.mcp.json)
2. Pass an environment variable as replacement pattern (e.g `"${env:MY_PASSWORD}"`)
3. Set the environment variable  to your value (`export MY_PASSWORD="123"`) and restart vscode
3. Start the mcp server
4. The environment variable will be set to `"${env:MY_PASSWORD}"` instead of the value of `$MY_PASSWORD` (123) 

Example of a working mcp server in the main user mcp.json file
```
{
    "mcpServers": {
        "elasticsearch": {
            "command": "docker",
            "args": [
                "run",
                "-i",
                "--rm",
                "-e",
                "ES_URL",
                "-e",
                "ES_USERNAME",
                "-e",
                "ES_PASSWORD",
                "-e",
                "ES_SSL_SKIP_VERIFY",
                "docker.elastic.co/mcp/elasticsearch",
                "stdio"
            ],
            "env": {
                "ES_URL": "https://myremoteserver:9200",
                "ES_USERNAME": "elastic",
                "ES_PASSWORD": "${env:MY_PASSWORD}",
                "ES_SSL_SKIP_VERIFY": "true"
            }
        }
    }
}
```
If I setup the same mcp server inside a plugin, the teplate substituition ("${env:MY_PASSWORD}") won't work.

This can be inspected by running the MCP server and doing a `docker inspect` in the container created

title: 1.115 Endgame(1)
body:
# Before Monday 6AM Zurich time

`@team`:
- Update endgame availability 
- Test plan items created 
- Milestone only has TPIs. All other issues need to be closed
- All closed issues in milestone labeled `on-testplan`, `bug`, or `verification-needed`
- Verification steps added to `bug` and `verification-needed` issues

# Monday morning  (Zurich)

`@endgame-champ`:
- [ ] Assign TPIs
  - [ ] Create TPI's for all verification needed bugs. Visit `Testing and Verification` on tools site, and generate groupings, then create TPIs. The TPI section below  will update with all of the generated items. 
- [ ] Pause automatic releases (this also ensures chat-pre-release isn't released) after 10am.
- [ ] In `vscode`, `vscode-distro`, `vscode-dev`
   - [ ] Branch following repositories to `git checkout -b release/x.y && git push -u origin release/x.y`: 
   - [ ] In `vscode`, bump up the version for main `npm version minor --no-git-tag-version && npm i`
- [ ] In `vscode-copilot-chat`
   - [ ] Branch following repositories to `git checkout -b release/a.b && git push -u origin release/a.b`: 
   - [ ] Bump up the version for main `npm version minor --no-git-tag-version && npm i`

# Monday morning (Redmond and Zurich)

`@team`:
- [Test plan items](https://github.com/issues?q=org%3Amicrosoft%20milestone%3A%221.115.0%22%20is%3Aissue%20is%3Aopen%20label%3Atestplan-item). All TPIs must be finished by noon. This includes verification TPIs.
- Make sure your TPIs are being tested and ping folks if to confirm they will finish by noon.

# Monday afternoon (Redmond and Zurich)

`@team`:
- Fix essential issues. Default to pushing to next iteration
- Release notes 

# Monday EOD Redmond time

`@team`:
- All issues including late fixes, are verified ([query](https://github.com/issues?q=org%3Amicrosoft+milestone%3A%221.115.0%22+is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed+reason%3Acompleted++label%3Abug+-label%3Averified+-label%3Aon-testplan+-label%3A*duplicate+-label%3Aduplicate+-label%3Ainvalid+-label%3A*as-designed+-label%3Aerror-telemetry+-label%3Averification-steps-needed+-label%3Az-author-verified+-label%3Aunreleased+-label%3A*not-reproducible+-label%3A*out-of-scope+sort%3Aupdated-asc))
- Release notes written

`@endgame-champ`:
- [ ] Create new builds so we can finish verification

# Tuesday by noon CET

`@team`:
- Fix essential issues. Default to pushing to next iteration
- Release notes 

`@endgame-champ`:
- [ ] Run [OSS tool](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-build-tools/tree/main/distro-tools)
- [ ] [Acknowledge third-party pull requests](https://tools.code.visualstudio.com/acknowledgement) in release notes.
- [ ] Acknowledge [issue trackers](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/wiki/Community-Triage---Credits#community-triage---role-based) from the community (do the copy-paste variant)
- [ ] Build and release insiders from release/<x.y>
- [ ] Build chat-prerelease from release/<a.b>
- [ ] Build chat-stable from release/<a.b> and release. Make sure this is published for at least 30 minutes before releasing stable to MSFT folks
- [ ] Build stable from release/<x.y> and release to MSFT folks
- [ ] Reenable automatic releases

# Wednesday
`@endgame-champ`:
- [ ] Stable starts rollout to everyone 
- [ ] Publish website 
- [ ] Create an official release 
  - [ ] Create a tag (make sure you pull the release branch first): `git tag <x.y.z>`
  - [ ] Push the tag: `git push origin <x.y.z>`
  - [ ] Create a GitHub release: [Open the GitHub tags](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tags), and click far right ... > Create Release. Use the version as title <x.y.z> and use the release link `https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v<x_y>` for the description
- [ ] Close milestone 
- [ ] Move all remaining issues to "On Deck"

title: Add suppressConfirmation option to updateWorkspaceFolders()
body:
## Problem

`updateWorkspaceFolders()` always shows a confirmation dialog when replacing the root folder because `enterWorkspace()` calls `stopExtensionHosts()`, which includes a user veto step. There is no way to suppress this programmatically.

Extensions that manage workspace folder transitions (worktree switching, session isolation, etc.) cannot do seamless folder swaps without the user clicking through a dialog every time.

## Context

PR #292783 by @bpasero already solved this for agent sessions — it calls `_doStopExtensionHosts()` directly to bypass the dialog in that context. This is the same pattern, generalized as an API option.

## Approach

Add an optional `suppressConfirmation` flag to `updateWorkspaceFolders()`. When set, `enterWorkspace()` calls `_doStopExtensionHosts()` instead of `stopExtensionHosts()`. Extension hosts still restart normally — only the dialog is skipped.

The change threads through: `vscode.d.ts` → `extHostWorkspace.ts` → `mainThreadWorkspace.ts` → `abstractWorkspaceEditingService.ts` → `workspaceEditingService.ts` (electron-browser).

## Current workaround

The [git-shell-helpers](https://github.com/RockyWearsAHat/github-shell-helpers) extension patches `workbench.desktop.main.js` at runtime to replace the `stopExtensionHosts()` call with `_doStopExtensionHosts()` in `enterWorkspace()`. This breaks on every VS Code update and requires re-patching.

## References

- PR #292783 — @bpasero's agent session implementation (same pattern)

title: Add headLabelOverride to Git Extension API
body:
## Problem

The Git extension's status bar branch label is derived from `HEAD`. Extensions that use worktrees to show different branches per window (or per chat session) can't override the displayed branch name without actually checking out the branch, which mutates working tree state and is slow.

## Context

Related upstream work:
- Issue #260706 by @sbatten — requesting better worktree visual distinction (assigned to @lszomoru)
- PR #305643 by @lszomoru — scaffolds a new Git extension API surface
- Issue #277163 — Git extension API for agent/CLI scenarios

## Approach

Add a `headLabelOverride` property to the Git extension's Repository model. When set, `get headLabel()` returns the override instead of the real HEAD name. Display-only — no git state is modified.

The change is ~10 lines in `extensions/git/src/repository.ts`:
- Check override before falling through to real HEAD logic in `get headLabel()` (line ~3209)
- Suppress or adapt the sync button when override is active

## Current workaround

The [git-shell-helpers](https://github.com/RockyWearsAHat/github-shell-helpers) extension patches the Git extension bundle (`extensions/git/dist/main.js`) to inject override logic into `get headLabel()` and `get command()`. This breaks on every VS Code update and requires re-patching.

## References

- Issue #260706 — worktree visual distinction
- PR #305643 — Git extension API scaffolding
- Issue #277163 — Git extension API for agent/CLI

title: Promote chat session focus events to stable API
body:
## Problem

`onDidChangeActiveChatPanelSessionResource` is gated behind the `chatParticipantPrivate` proposed API. Using it requires `enabledApiProposals` in `package.json` + manual `argv.json` edits + VS Code restart. It can't ship via the Marketplace.

Extensions that maintain per-conversation state (branch sessions, context files, tool configs) need to detect chat session switches. This is a basic lifecycle event — similar to `onDidChangeActiveTextEditor` or `onDidChangeActiveTerminal`.

## Context

The chat session infrastructure is being actively rebuilt:
- PR #304532 — "Chat Session Customizations initial Sketch"
- PR #305297 — "Multi chat support"  
- PR #305730 — "Session types changes and smarter chat to session mapping"
- Issue #305853 by @wycats — requesting `chatSessionResource` exposure (assigned to @jrieken)

## Approach

Promote the existing event to stable. The implementation already works via `$acceptActiveChatSession` IPC — this is just moving it out from behind the proposed API gate.

1. Move event registration from `chatParticipantPrivate` to the stable `window` namespace
2. Remove `checkProposedApiEnabled` gate in `extHost.api.impl.ts` (lines ~1055-1061)
3. Add `activeChatSessionUri` getter for current value (not just events)
4. Add stable declarations in `vscode.d.ts`

No new IPC, no new renderer code. Promotion only.

## Current workaround

```json
// ~/.vscode/argv.json
{ "enable-proposed-api": ["RockyWearsAHat.git-shell-helpers"] }
```

Works but requires manual setup and can't be distributed.

## References

- Issue #305853 — @wycats requesting chat session resource exposure
- PR #305730 — Session types changes
- PR #305297 — Multi chat support

title: Feature Request: Sync GitHub Copilot Chat History Across Devices
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Summary

This is a continuation of the discussion from the now-archived repository:
**[microsoft/vscode-copilot-release#991 – sync github copilot chat history across devices](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-release/issues/991)**

That issue was closed as "not planned / out-of-scope" and the repository was archived on March 23, 2026 with a note to redirect feedback here. Given the significant community interest (79 👍 / 120 ❤️) and continued activity up until archival, I'm opening this issue to carry the discussion forward.

---

## Problem Statement

GitHub Copilot chat history is stored locally and is **not synchronized across devices**. For developers who work on multiple machines (e.g., a laptop and a desktop), this means:

- Past conversations and context are siloed per device
- The same prompts must be re-entered to reconstruct context
- Valuable debugging sessions, architectural discussions, and iterative problem-solving threads are effectively lost when switching machines

This is especially frustrating given that:
1. **GitHub Copilot on the web and GitHub Mobile** already maintain conversation history tied to the GitHub account
2. **Settings Sync** already handles extensions, settings, keybindings, and UI state — chat history feels like a natural addition
3. Competing tools (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code) face the same limitation and users are actively seeking solutions

---

## Desired Behavior

Copilot chat history should be optionally syncable across devices, either:

- **Via Settings Sync** (the existing VS Code sync mechanism), or
- **Via GitHub account** (as a server-side store linked to the user's GitHub identity), or
- **Via a dedicated export/import mechanism** as a minimum viable fallback

---

## Prior Discussion Highlights

From [microsoft/vscode-copilot-release#991](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-copilot-release/issues/991):

- [@isidorn (Collaborator)](https://github.com/isidorn) suggested Settings Sync as a candidate mechanism (Dec 2024)
- [@sandy081 (Member)](https://github.com/sandy081) noted that "Syncing state is supported by Settings Sync. It is up to the owner of the state to sync or not." — implying this is **technically feasible**, but no owner has stepped up to implement it
- Community continued asking for this feature until the very last week before archival

---

## Additional Context

- The original issue was open for **2+ years** with sustained engagement
- The `*out-of-scope` label was applied, but the repository archival and redirect to this repo suggests scope may have changed
- This feature is available in GitHub's own web and mobile Copilot interfaces, creating an **inconsistent experience** across the GitHub ecosystem

---

## React / Vote

If you'd like to see this feature, please react with 👍 on this issue.

body: I've actually always wanted this in VS Code too: clicking the preview button on a markdown file should just swap out in place, as opposed to doing side by side. Often I just want to toggle between the two, but this becomes especially apparent when reading a plan or spec that I've clicked on in the chat from a pill in the Sessions app. Maybe the artifact viewer will make this flow opinionated, and I won't even see the text version of a plan and just the rendered markdown.

title: Show +/- line diff stats in the Source Control panel
body: ### Feature Request When reviewing changes in the Source Control panel before committing, there's no quick way to see the total number of lines added and removed across all changed files. ### Proposed behavior Show a compact +X / -Y summary somewhere in the Source Control panel (e.g. near the Changes header or the Commit button area) similar to how Git shows these stats in the terminal. ### Reason: A small visual cue helps you gauge the size of your changeset at a glance before committing, useful for catching unexpectedly large diffs early.

title: `send_to_terminal` progress message repeats first question when accepting all defaults in interactive commands
body:
## Bug

When an interactive command like `npm init` is run and the user accepts all defaults via the `askQuestions` carousel, every `send_to_terminal` progress message displays the first question's text (e.g. "Package name?") instead of the correct question for each prompt.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session in default approvals mode
2. Ask the agent to run `npm init` in a terminal
3. The agent detects the interactive prompts and shows an `askQuestions` carousel with multiple questions (package name, version, description, entry point, etc.)
4. Accept all defaults by leaving every field empty and submitting the carousel
5. The agent sends each default answer via `send_to_terminal` (pressing Enter for each prompt)

## Expected Behavior

Each `send_to_terminal` progress message should show the corresponding question:

- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name?)
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: version?)
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: description?)
- …

## Actual Behavior

Every progress message repeats the first question:

- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- Pressed `Enter` in terminal (replying to: Package name? (default: @xterm/xterm))
- …

## Cause

`_getQuestionContextForTerminal` matches the sent command text against carousel answer values to find the corresponding question. When all answers are identical (empty string for defaults), the loop iterates questions in order and always matches the first one.

## Fix

Use positional matching: count prior `send_to_terminal` tool invocations after the carousel in the response parts to determine the question index, rather than relying solely on answer-value matching.

title: Copilot Chat local models do not populate Context Window usage even when backend usage and model limits are available
body:
### Copilot Chat version

0.47.2026042905

### VS Code version

1.119.0-insider

### OS

Windows 11 Pro 25H2

### Regression?

Unknown

### Problem description

GitHub Copilot Chat in Visual Studio Code (VS Code) can successfully use local models through the built-in `ollama` and `customoai` providers, but the Context Window usage area stays empty.

The visible behavior is:

- chat requests succeed
- the local model replies normally
- the model limit is shown in the Context Window area
- but the used-context ring/graph stays gray and the tooltip remains at `0 / <max tokens>`

On my machine, one tested example showed `0 / 294K tokens` for a working local chat session.

### Why I believe this is a real product bug and not just a backend quirk

I am routing the model through a local compatibility proxy so I can control the transport behavior precisely.

That proxy can emit final streamed usage in an OpenAI-compatible shape, including:

- `prompt_tokens`
- `completion_tokens`
- `total_tokens`

The local model configuration also provides token-window metadata such as:

- `maxInputTokens`
- `maxOutputTokens`

So the backend-side ingredients appear to exist, and the user interface (UI) already knows the maximum context size. The missing part seems to be the path that should carry usage into the chat response model that drives the Context Window widget.

### Reproduction steps

1. Configure a local model for Copilot Chat using either:
   - the built-in `customoai` provider with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or
   - the built-in `ollama` provider backed by a local server or proxy.
2. Make sure the configured model has valid context-window metadata such as `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens`.
3. Start a new Copilot Chat session with that local model.
4. Send a prompt that clearly consumes non-trivial context.
5. Open or inspect the Context Window usage area.

### Expected behavior

The Context Window usage area should show non-zero usage for the request, similar to hosted models, once a reply has completed and usage information is available.

### Actual behavior

The Context Window usage area remains empty / gray, and the tooltip stays at `0 / <max tokens>` even though the chat response completed successfully.

### Additional technical notes

I looked through the public source and found a few things that may help narrow the issue:

- the widget appears to render from chat response usage plus model token limits
- local models do appear to have model-limit metadata available
- the transport side can produce final usage information
- the likely gap appears to be in how local language-model-provider results flow into the chat response usage model

I also tried a machine-local unsupported experiment patching the installed runtime to preserve provider result metadata through both worker-based and node-based language-model bridges. That did not make the widget light up, which suggests the missing seam may be deeper than a single dropped completion result, or that the active local-model response object still never receives the usage payload expected by the widget.

I am not asking maintainers to support local patching. I am including that note only because it may help narrow where the missing usage handoff is.

### Notes

I can provide a minimal local endpoint setup if needed, but this seems reproducible in principle with any local model path where:

- chat works
- model token limits are known
- backend usage is available

The problem is specifically that the Context Window usage UI never reflects that usage.

title: Git commit message generation is promptFiltered when commitMessageGeneration.instructions contains Japanese text
body:
## Summary
Git commit message generation in VS Code Source Control stops working when `github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGeneration.instructions` contains Japanese text. The UI appears to do nothing, but the Copilot Chat log shows `promptFiltered`.

## Environment
- VS Code: 1.119.0
- Commit: 8b640eef5a6c6089c029249d48efa5c99adf7d51
- Architecture: x64
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.47.0
- Remote environment: VS Code Server on Linux

## Repro steps
1. Set this in workspace settings:

   ```json
   "github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGeneration.instructions": [
     {
       "text": "コミットメッセージは日本語で、1行目に変更内容を簡潔に書いてください。"
     }
   ]
   ```

2. Stage a small change, even only `.vscode/settings.json` or a CSS file.
3. Use Source Control's Copilot commit message generation.
4. No commit message is generated.

## Expected behavior
A commit message should be generated, ideally following the custom instruction.

## Actual behavior
No message is shown in the Source Control input. The Copilot Chat log reports `promptFiltered`.

## Log excerpts

```text
[GitExtensionServiceImpl] Successfully registered Git commit message provider.
Copilot Chat: 0.47.0, VS Code: 1.119.0
ccreq:... | promptFiltered | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | ...ms | [gitCommitMessageGenerator]
```

This happened repeatedly with different staged file subsets.

## Workaround
Setting the instruction to an empty array makes commit message generation work again:

```json
"github.copilot.chat.commitMessageGeneration.instructions": []
```

So the staged diff itself does not appear to be the trigger. The issue seems related to Japanese custom commit message instructions being included in the prompt.

title: Source Control Graph hover truncates commit metadata when commit message is long
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem

In the built-in Source Control Graph, hovering over a commit shows a tooltip with the commit message and commit metadata such as branch/tag/ref information.

When the commit message is long, the tooltip truncation/cutoff can hide the metadata at the bottom. This makes the hover less useful because the high-value metadata is not visible unless the commit message is short enough to fit.

## Expected behavior

The hover should prioritize commit metadata over the long commit message.

A better layout would be:

1. Show commit metadata at the top:
   - commit hash
   - author
   - date
   - branch/ref/tag information

2. Show the commit subject/body preview below that, truncated if needed.

3. Optionally provide an action/button/link to open the full commit message/details in a popup, side panel, or commit details view.

## Actual behavior

Long commit messages can consume the tooltip space and cause branch/tag/ref metadata to be clipped or unavailable.

## Why this matters

Branch/tag/ref metadata is usually compact and high-value when inspecting a graph. Long commit messages are variable-length and should not be able to push important metadata out of view.

## Area

Source Control Graph / Git commit hover tooltip

title: Adding the first root folder to an empty-window workspace restarts the extension host, killing in-progress Copilot Chat sessions
body:
### Description

Type: Bug / UX papercut

VS Code version: 
Version: 1.123.0 (user setup)
Commit: 6a44c352bd24569c417e530095901b649960f9f8
Date: 2026-06-03T11:29:03+02:00

Node.js: 24.15.0
V8: 14.8.178.14-electron.0
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200
OS: Windows

Describe the bug
When a window has no folder open (empty workspace) and you add a folder via Add Folder to Workspace (workbench.action.addRootFolder), VS Code transitions the workspace and restarts the extension host. This triggers a "Please confirm restart of extensions — A session is in progress" dialog and, if confirmed, terminates the active GitHub Copilot Chat session.

Steps to reproduce

Launch VS Code with no folder open (empty window).
Start a Copilot Chat session and do some work.
Add Folder to Workspace → pick any folder.
Observe the "Please confirm restart of extensions" dialog; confirming restarts the extension host and loses the chat session.
Expected behavior
Adding a folder to an existing window should not force an extension-host restart that destroys in-progress extension state (like a Copilot Chat conversation). Going from 0→1 folders should behave like N→N+1 folders, which does not restart the host.

Actual behavior
The 0→1 folder transition (empty window → single-root/multi-root workspace) restarts the extension host, killing the chat session. There's no path to mount the first folder without losing session state.

Impact
Users who start a chat in an empty window — e.g., during design/planning before a repo exists — must choose between keeping their conversation or working with the folder mounted in the Explorer. Long planning sessions are lost on folder add.

Possible improvements

Preserve extension-host state across the empty→single-folder transition (avoid the restart), or
Allow extensions to persist/restore session state across the transition, or
Make the restart non-destructive for chat (serialize + rehydrate the conversation).

editor.insertSnippet() still destroys active snippet session tabstops (regression from #214757, misclosed)
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No — this is an API regression affecting extensions that call `editor.insertSnippet()`.

- VS Code Version: 1.86.0+ through current (regression introduced in 1.86, works correctly in 1.85.2)
- OS Version: All platforms

## Summary

`editor.insertSnippet()` called from an extension while a snippet session is active destroys the outer session's remaining tabstops. This is a regression from 1.86.

This was previously reported as #214757, which was closed as a duplicate of #63129. However, **these are unrelated issues**: #63129 is about snippet auto-indentation (fixed in #234858 by exposing `keepWhitespace`), not tabstop destruction. Since #214757 is locked, I'm opening a new issue.

## Root cause

In 1.86, `mainThreadEditor.ts` was refactored to route extension API `insertSnippet()` calls through `snippetController.apply(edits[])` instead of `snippetController.insert(template)`.

In `snippetController2.ts`, `_doInsert()` has this guard:

```typescript
if (this._session && typeof template !== 'string') {
    this.cancel();
}
```

The `apply()` path passes an array, hitting `this.cancel()` and destroying the active session. The `insert()` path passes a string, hitting `this._session.merge()` which properly nests the new snippet. The merge infrastructure (`OneSnippet.merge()`, `_nestingLevel`, `_renormalizePlaceholderIndices()`) is fully implemented and works — the API bridge just stopped using it.

## Impact

This breaks any extension that programmatically inserts snippets during editing:
- [HyperSnips](https://github.com/draivin/hsnips/issues/189) (77 comments, open since Feb 2024)
- [HyperSnips #157](https://github.com/draivin/hsnips/issues/157)
- [LTeX](https://github.com/valentjn/vscode-ltex) and other language extensions

## Fix

I have a PR ready: #322008

The fix is ~5 lines: route single-edit `insertSnippet()` calls back through `snippetController.insert()` (the merge path), falling back to `apply()` only for multi-range edits that cannot be merged.

cc @jrieken 

---

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install any extension that calls `editor.insertSnippet()` in response to typing (e.g. [HyperSnips](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=draivin.hsnips))
2. Trigger a snippet with multiple tabstops (e.g. a snippet that expands to `\int_{$1}^{$2} $3 \,d$4`)
3. While the cursor is at `$1`, type text that triggers the extension to call `editor.insertSnippet()` with a simple replacement
4. Press Tab — expected: cursor moves to `$2`. Actual: snippet session is destroyed, Tab inserts a tab character.

This works correctly in VS Code 1.85.2 and earlier.

---

This issue was researched and analysed with the assistance of [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/claude-code) (Claude Opus 4.6).

body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.56.2026070305 (prod)
- VS Code Version: 1.128.0-insider 
- OS Version: Windows 11 Home, win32 x 64
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Copilot Chat Agent mode / chat requests
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.5 
- Logs:
  - Copilot diagnostics collected via “GitHub Copilot: Collect Diagnostics”

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code Insiders and start a Copilot Chat request in Agent mode.
2. Send a normal coding/task request that should use tools or reasoning.
3. Copilot repeatedly gets stuck showing “Thinking”, “Reasoning”, or “Analyzing” and does not progress to a useful response or tool action.
4. Restarting/retrying may create new sessions, but the behavior has happened repeatedly throughout the day.

Additional diagnostics:

- GitHub account: jadetrailenterprises
- Active fetcher: Electron fetch
- Network diagnostics show HTTP 200 for:
  - https://api.github.com
  - https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com/_ping
  - https://proxy.individual.githubcopilot.com/_ping
  - telemetry endpoints
- IPv6 DNS lookups returned ENOTFOUND, but IPv4 connectivity succeeded.

title: Modernize: Copilot/circle icons too large; match adjacent text size
body:
## Feedback

> maybe just a me thing, but i think the icons are a tad bit big here (the copilot icon and the circle).
>
> i'd like if they were the same font size as the text so they fit a bit nicer with the text perhaps?

**Source**: #ws-modernize-ui — Justin Chen on 2026-06-22 ([Slack](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C0AM349P43S/p1782147978039499))
**Reactions**: 👍 ×1

---

## Context

As part of the UI Modernization effort, iconography in the Agents/chat surface should feel visually balanced with adjacent text. The Copilot icon and the accompanying circle indicator currently read as slightly oversized relative to the label text they sit next to, making the row feel a touch heavy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Copilot icon and circle indicator are sized to visually match the adjacent text font size
- [ ] The change is verified against both Dark and Light 2026 themes
- [ ] No clipping or vertical misalignment is introduced in the row

title: Modernize: Add a compact mode option for smaller laptop screens
body:
## Feedback

> I brought this up previously, but making more focussed feedback here. I would love an option for a 'compact' mode.
> The padding between the windows are great in my large monitor. But when I'm on my laptop, I feel like I am losing screen real-estate that I would choose to have over window padding. (it feels worse than it is because I go from like a wide screen to a 14 inch)

**Source**: #workbench-refresh-feedback — VB on 2026-06-26 ([Slack](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C0BCLPWGMJQ/p1782486168517709))

Related report — tyler on 2026-06-26 ([Slack](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C0BCLPWGMJQ/p1782516460985979)), 👍 ×1:

> just so much padding on my 16in mbp...

> **Thread — Lee Murray:** I have reduced the gaps from `12px` to `8px` — anything smaller & it starts to feel too cramped. Please try it out & let me know if it helps

---

## Context

The Modern UI window padding is well-received on large external monitors but costs valuable horizontal/vertical real estate on smaller laptop screens (14–16"). While default gaps were reduced from 12px to 8px, multiple users want an explicit, opt-in "compact" mode that trims inter-panel padding further for constrained displays without everyone self-hosting individual settings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provide an opt-in compact mode (single setting) that reduces Modern UI inter-panel padding for smaller screens
- [ ] Compact mode is discoverable and does not require manually tuning multiple individual settings
- [ ] Default (non-compact) spacing is unchanged

title: [Bug]: ESM ASAR loader strict path check fails when launching via NTFS Junction (Scoop compatibility)
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->

- Version: 1.129.0-insider
- Commit: 29d19ddd1af725baf537b6b328843bcdc2d29ba1
- OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200

### Description

When launching VS Code Insiders via an NTFS Directory Junction (a common setup for Windows package managers like Scoop), the application fails to start due to an ESM module resolution error for internal packages (e.g., `Cannot find package '@vscode/policy-watcher'`).

The application runs perfectly fine when launched directly from the physical version directory, but fails when launched through a junction point (e.g., a `current` directory link).

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install the [latest VS Code Insiders](https://github.com/ScoopInstaller/Versions/blob/8b04b6f2a9c368cece252a782164fd995e2d38e3/bucket/vscode-insiders.json#L2) via Scoop: `scoop install Versions/vscode-insiders`.
2. Navigate to the `current` directory and double-click `Code - Insiders.exe` (fails to launch). However, double-clicking `Code - Insiders.exe` inside the physical version directory (e.g., `1.129.0-1783592085744`) launches the app normally.
3. Execute the following command in the terminal:
   ```powershell
   ┏[ ~]
   └─> & "D:\Software\Scoop\Local\apps\vscode-insiders\current\Code - Insiders.exe"

   [main 2026-07-09T19:41:10.475Z] Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@vscode/policy-watcher' imported from D:\Software\Scoop\Local\apps\vscode-insiders\1.129.0-1783592085744\29d19ddd1a\resources\app\out\main.js
       at Object.getPackageJSONURL (node:internal/modules/package_json_reader:301:9)
       at packageResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:780:81)
       at moduleResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:871:18)
       at defaultResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/resolve:1004:11)
       at nextResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/hooks:785:28)
       at resolve (data:text/javascript;base64,CglpbXB...=:182:10)
       at nextResolve (node:internal/modules/esm/hooks:785:28)
       at AsyncLoaderHooksOnLoaderHookWorker.resolve (node:internal/modules/esm/hooks:269:30)
       at MessagePort.handleMessage (node:internal/modules/esm/worker:251:24)
       at [nodejs.internal.kHybridDispatch] (node:internal/event_target:843:20)
   ```

---

This issue first appeared after upgrading to version [1.129.0-1783530600056](https://github.com/ScoopInstaller/Versions/commit/13a92f4413c9e956ef79043361acf30bde04aafd). Below are the potential causes I identified by using AI to analyze the changes between commits 926982696e5076805ed790713fe2417a6eb2c7c2 and 29ebca462ca8c04401d6c6f8aa50793abe8fa58d. I hope this information helps identify and resolve the issue:

````
This regression appears to be introduced in the recent ESM bootstrap refactor (specifically in `src/bootstrap-esm.ts`). The custom ESM loader hook performs a strict string comparison to ensure modules are loaded from within the app resources:

```javascript
// In src/bootstrap-esm.ts
try { parentPath = normalizeDriveLetter(fileURLToPath(context.parentURL)); } catch { parentPath = undefined; }
if (parentPath && parentPath.startsWith(resourcesPath)) { 
    // ACCEPT 
}
```

Node.js's native ESM resolution automatically resolves directory junctions/symlinks to their real physical paths. Therefore, `context.parentURL` (and subsequently `parentPath`) contains the resolved physical path.

However, `resourcesPath` is initialized based on the launch path, which retains the junction path alias. Because the junction path and the real physical path do not match as strings, `parentPath.startsWith(resourcesPath)` evaluates to `false`. The loader incorrectly treats the module as an "outside app resource" and rejects the ASAR internal module loading.
````

title: Agent host networking: align transient retry behavior and remove unnecessary Fetch Content-Length header
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: main (current development branch)
- OS Version: Windows 11 x64

## Steps to Reproduce

### Issue 1 – Missing transient retry codes

1. Configure `AgentHostRequestService` so that an idempotent request (`GET`) fails with an `ECONNRESET` error.
2. Observe that the request fails immediately instead of being retried.

The current retry logic retries several transient network failures (for example `ECONNREFUSED`) but does not treat `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, or `ETIMEDOUT` as transient.

Other networking components in the repository already retry these error codes, resulting in inconsistent retry behavior across the codebase.

---

### Issue 2 – Fetch branch sets `Content-Length`

`OtlpHttpForwarder` sets the `content-length` request header when using the Fetch implementation.

According to the Fetch specification, `Content-Length` is a forbidden request header and is automatically computed by the runtime. The manually specified value is ignored by compliant Fetch implementations, making the header unnecessary in this code path.

The existing `http.request()` path should continue setting `content-length` because Node's HTTP APIs require it.

## Expected Result

- Retry behavior should be consistent with other networking components for transient connection-reset style failures.
- The Fetch implementation should rely on the runtime to compute `Content-Length` automatically while leaving the `http.request()` implementation unchanged.

## Actual Result

- `ECONNRESET`, `EPIPE`, and `ETIMEDOUT` are not retried by `AgentHostRequestService`.
- `OtlpHttpForwarder` explicitly sets `content-length` in the Fetch path even though Fetch implementations compute it automatically.

## Additional Information

I have implemented fixes for both issues and added regression tests for the retry behavior.

title: Wrapped tabs: Don't stretch the last tab to fill the remaining row
body: # Wrapped tabs: Last tab should not expand and overlap tab actions ## Problem When using these settings: ```json "workbench.editor.showTabs": "multiple", "workbench.editor.wrapTabs": true, "workbench.editor.tabSizing": "fit" ``` and enough open editors for the tab bar to wrap onto multiple rows, the last tab in each row is stretched to fill the remaining horizontal space. The stretched last tab leaves no empty area at the end of wrapped rows. As a consequence: - on the last row, the tab's close button ends up underneath the **More Actions** (`...`) button, making it not clickable. - this also removes the empty tab strip area that can normally be double-clicked to create a new untitled editor when tabs are displayed on a single row. ### Current vs. expected behavior **Current** ```text ┌─────┬─────┬────────────────────────────┐ │ foo │ bar │ baz │ ├─────┴─────┴────────────────────────────┤ │ qux │ └────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Expected** ```text ┌─────┬─────┬────────────────────────────┐ │ foo │ bar │ baz │ ├─────┬──────────────────────────────────┤ │ qux │ │ └─────┴──────────────────────────────────┘ ``` The last tab of the last row should keep its natural width, leaving the remaining tab strip area empty. ## Proposed solution Provide a way to prevent the last wrapped tab from stretching to fill the remaining horizontal space, either through a new setting or as an additional `tabSizing` mode. For example: ```json "workbench.editor.fillLastWrappedTab": false ``` ## Benefits - Prevents the last tab's close button from being unclickable behind the **More Actions** button. - Restores the ability to double-click the empty tab strip to create a new untitled editor. - Gives users a choice between the current appearance and a more compact layout. - Matches the expectation that tabs using `"fit"` sizing should only occupy the space required by their content. ## Alternatives considered - Disabling wrapped tabs is not desirable, as it replaces wrapping with horizontal scrolling. - `"workbench.editor.tabSizing": "shrink"` leaves empty space, but it truncates tab titles. - `"workbench.editor.tabSizing": "fixed"` keeps all tabs on a single row instead of wrapping. - Using keyboard shortcuts (e.g. `Ctrl+N` and `Ctrl+W` for "new" and "close" tab) is a workaround but does not restore the existing mouse interactions. ## Additional context This is primarily a UX enhancement rather than an aesthetic preference. The goal is to preserve the usability of the tab strip while using wrapped tabs. Originally I opened this as a feature request for the ability to keep the double clicking, and then I noticed the "close tab" button is also unclickable, so I added that to my post.

title: Starting a new Copilot Agent Host session (Editor or Agents Window) or creating a new `chat` in Agents Window is slow
body:
I found a reproducible >1s delay when starting a new Agent Host Session or creating a new `chat` in Agents Window from an existing session.
Root cause: BYOK model enumeration includes the main-process infrastructure connection (`clientId='agentHost'`),
This infrastructure/logging connection/process does not expose the renderer BYOK reverse channel.

This causes a 1s timeout during `listModels()` which is called when constructing the Copilot CLI SDK options object.
This in turn causes the >1s delay

Proposed short-term mitigation in `agentHostMain.ts`:
```
if (byokLmEnabled && byokLmBridgeRegistry && clientId !== 'agentHost') {
    const byokLmConnection = createAgentHostClientByokLmConnection(getChannel(AGENT_HOST_CLIENT_BYOK_LM_CHANNEL));
    connectionStore.add(byokLmBridgeRegistry.register(clientId, byokLmConnection));
}
```
Note: `listModels` currently refreshes models on all connections  via `Promise.all`,
This solution is filtering by `clientId !== 'agentHost'` is fragile feels hacky

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
### Type: Performance Issue / Regression

**Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?**: Yes (reproduces on `--disable-extensions`, and confirmed via Extension Host CPU Profile that the extension host is ~96% idle during the freeze — see attached cpuprofile)

### VS Code Version
- Broken: 1.128.0 x64
- Last known good: 1.125.1 x64

### OS
Linux Mint 22.3 Cinnamon (X11), NVIDIA driver 32.0.16.1074, GPU: RTX 5060

### Environment
- Dual monitor: primary 2560x1440 @ 200Hz (no rotation), secondary 1920x1080 @ 75Hz (rotated)
- Also reproduces with a single monitor
- Reproduces with GPU acceleration ON and OFF (`--disable-hardware-acceleration`)
- Reproduces with VRR/G-Sync ON and OFF
- Reproduces at DPI scale 100%, 130%, and 140% (font/window zoom, not just OS scale)
- pnpm monorepo workspace: ~6,700 TS files across 4 projects (NestJS backend, 2x Next.js apps, shared package)
- Confirmed NOT caused by: git extension (reproduces with `code --disable-extension vscode.git`), any 3rd-party extension, GPU driver/compositor (ruled out via cross-app resize test on Nautilus/Firefox — no lag there), system resources (RAM/swap/temps all confirmed normal during freeze)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a large multi-root/monorepo workspace with several editor groups/tabs open (4+ splits)
2. Drag-resize the OS-level VS Code window (or rapidly drag an internal sash/panel divider)
3. Observe stuttering/frozen UI during the resize, worse with more open editor groups and with a large number of modified files in Source Control (700+ in our repro)

### What i found (Performance trace attached)
Captured via Help → Toggle Developer Tools → Performance tab during a window resize (see attached `trace.zip`).

The main renderer thread (`CrRendererMain`) shows repeated `mousemove`-triggered `FunctionCall` events (`workbench.desktop.main.js`, minified function `i`) each taking 350–500ms. Inside a single such call we counted **15–20 sequential `UpdateLayoutTree` passes (~20-24ms each, ~330ms total)**, plus a full V8 Major GC cycle running synchronously inside the handler (GC_MC_MARK/GC_MC_EVACUATE etc., ~35ms+). This looks like forced synchronous layout (layout thrashing) scaling with the number of open editor groups/tabs — closing extra tabs/splits measurably reduces (but doesn't eliminate) the severity.

Extension Host CPU Profile (attached, `cpuprofile.zip`) taken during the same freeze shows the extension host at 96.2% idle throughout, with no sustained CPU spike — ruling out extensions (including the built-in Git extension) as the cause.

### Regression
This got noticeably worse in a recent update — reverting to a ~3-week-old build (`1.125.1`) reduces the issue to a minor, tolerable degradation; the current stable build (`1.128.0`) makes it severe enough to make resizing the window near-unusable.

### Possibly related
- #165441 (janky resize with multiple editor groups, includes a similar Chrome performance profile)
- #169142 (slow window resizing performance)
- #26566 (resizing side panel very slow — forced layout confirmed by maintainers back in 2017)
- #306246 (resize stutter, Wayland/tiled — same class of issue on a different compositor)

Attached: `trace.zip` (Performance trace during resize), `cpuprofile.zip` (Extension Host profile, showing extensions are not the cause)

title: Status bar: balance vertical spacing
body:
## Feedback

> It seems like there is extra vertical space above the status bar. I would have expected the gap below the bottom to the bottom of the window and above to the border of the panel/file tree to be the same

**Source**: #ws-modernize-ui — Connor Peet on 2026-07-13
**Reactions**: eyes ×1

**Attachments**: https://vscodeteam.slack.com/files/U0ALN6MH067/F0BH4002E8Z/image.png

> Maybe #workbench-refresh-feedback is more appropriate but <@U08DC5MKQFR>

---

## Context

The modernized workbench leaves uneven visual space around the status bar. The bottom edge should feel consistently inset relative to adjacent workbench parts, including the panel and file tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The vertical gap above the status bar matches the gap below it at the window edge.
- [ ] The status-bar spacing remains visually balanced next to the panel and file tree.
- [ ] The spacing is verified in the modernized workbench layout.

title: Workbench layout: offer compact density
body:
## Feedback

> <@U08DC5MKQFR> have we considered also having a compact mode of this new design? We have a lot of users which work on small screens and get very annoyed when we waste space in the UI, they always ask for a compact version of our UX/layout features. I wonder if we could have some setting (`window.density.layout`) which when set to `compact` removes the spacing between the cards, uses the compact activity bar and maybe also the compact tab bar (`window.density.editorTabHeight`).

**Source**: #workbench-refresh-feedback — Benjamin Simmonds on 2026-07-14
**Reactions**: heavy_plus_sign ×1, 100 ×1, eyes ×1

> Let me do some experiments to understand feasibility. My concern is that if we introduce a variety of densities, we end up multiplying the investment in maintenance. Perhaps we can shave off a couple of pixels within the gaps & maybe even drop the non-editor panel borders to reclaim space
>
> I feel like these larger gaps are also less usable because in order to use a mouse to drag the panel size, one needs to catch an invisible vertical center of the gap, while eg in slack, it's just a line to drag
>
> it's definitely not "delightful" for me

---

## Context

The UI Modernization layout needs to remain efficient on smaller screens. Feedback calls for either a compact density option or targeted reductions to inter-part gaps and borders, while preserving maintainable layout behavior and easy panel resizing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Smaller-screen users can select or receive a more space-efficient workbench layout.
- [ ] The compact treatment reduces unnecessary inter-part gaps without impairing panel resizing.
- [ ] Activity-bar and tab sizing remain coherent with the selected density.

title: Improve visibility of blocking input prompts requiring user interaction
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem

VS Code occasionally displays blocking input prompts (for example InputBox or Quick Input) that require the user to enter information before an operation can continue.

These prompts are surprisingly easy to miss.

The prompt typically appears at the very top of the window, while the user's attention is often focused somewhere else:

- the integrated terminal
- the editor
- the Debug Console
- the Output panel
- an extension view
- another part of the workbench

When the prompt is overlooked, the running operation simply waits for user input. From the user's perspective, it often appears as if VS Code, the terminal, or an extension has frozen.

## Examples

This can happen in many situations, including but not limited to:

- Git authentication
- SSH passphrase requests
- Authentication dialogs from extensions
- API key prompts
- Extension configuration prompts
- Any extension using `window.showInputBox()`

The issue is therefore not specific to Git but affects any workflow that relies on blocking user input.

## Expected Behavior

Whenever VS Code is waiting for required user input, it should provide a much more noticeable indication that attention is required.

The exact implementation is up to the VS Code team, but the goal is that users immediately recognize:

> "The current operation is waiting for my input."

## Why This Matters

Missing the prompt can easily lead users to believe that:

- the terminal has frozen,
- Git or another tool is hanging,
- an extension has stopped responding,
- VS Code has become unresponsive,
- or a network operation is taking unusually long.

This results in unnecessary waiting, cancelled operations, repeated commands, and avoidable confusion.

## Possible Ideas

These are only examples—any solution that improves discoverability would help:

- Highlight the prompt more prominently.
- Draw temporary attention to it with an animation.
- Display an indicator near the component that initiated the request (for example the terminal).
- Show a temporary notification that user input is required.
- Optionally play a notification sound.
- Improve accessibility announcements for blocking prompts.

The important part is not the specific implementation, but making it immediately obvious that VS Code is waiting for user interaction.

title: Cross-origin worker execution vulnerability
body:
## VS Code - Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.128.0 and earlier versions where, if you host a standalone VS Code server via `code serve-web` or similar, an attacker with knowledge of the domain could retrieve the connection token used for the server.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.128.1**. The fix (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/236fa7d8ea86f0f4261df38e1a17b3c7e7002bd0) mitigates this attack by performing validation of the origin of webview messages.

### Workarounds

Do not use `code serve-web` or similar on versions of VS Code <=1.128.0

### References
* The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/236fa7d8ea86f0f4261df38e1a17b3c7e7002bd0
* An advisory for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-v282-cxqj-xgj4
* MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-57102

title: VS Code - Workspace Trust Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
body:
## VS Code - Workspace Trust Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

A security feature bypass vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.128.0 and earlier versions where, under certain conditions, specially crafted notebook content could bypass security restrictions in Restricted Mode.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.128.1**. The fix mitigates this attack by improving how untrusted notebook content is handled.

### Workarounds

Do not open notebooks from untrusted sources on versions of VS Code <=1.128.0.

### References

* The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/bc2d56c6f8da22a4bd31f741fcb034208770f158
* An advisory for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-9mw4-h26x-gfxw
* MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-57101

title: Copilot token secret exfiltration vulnerability
body:
## VS Code - Secret exfiltration vulnerability

A secret exfiltration vulnerability exists in VS Code 1.128.0 and earlier versions where, if you open a malicous workspace that contains hidden advanced copilot settings in the workspace settings your Copilot token (30m lifetime) may be sent to a malicious upstream server.

### Patches

The fix is available starting with **VS Code 1.128.1**. The fix (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f05bcd1aa29cff28a62fe137b4a16fec9393f31b) mitigates this attack by only respecting hidden advanced settings in a trusted workspace.

### Workarounds

Use external tooling to inspect workspace settings for any malicious URLs prior to opening an untrusted workspace on versions of VS Code <=1.128.0

### References
* The patch for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f05bcd1aa29cff28a62fe137b4a16fec9393f31b
* An advisory for this can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/security/advisories/GHSA-wr9x-42j2-jvh3
* MSRC details for this can be found at https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-47282

title: gitCommitMessageGenerator Consistently Fails and Returns Error 422
body:
Type: Bug Environment GitHub Copilot Chat extension: 0.56.0 VS Code: 1.128.0 OS: Linux Copilot token SKU: free_educational_quota Model used for feature: gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 Feature: gitCommitMessageGenerator (Source Control "Generate Commit Message" button) Summary Clicking "Generate Commit Message" in the Source Control panel fails 100% of the time with a 422 Unprocessable Entity from the Copilot backend. Started suddenly a few days ago with no local configuration changes. The personal account setting "Copilot-generated commit messages" is confirmed Enabled at github.com/settings/copilot. Steps to reproduce Sign in to VS Code with a GitHub account on the free_educational_quota Copilot SKU. Open any git repo with at least one uncommitted change (reproduced both in an existing project and in a brand-new blank repo with a single test file — rules out repo/org content-exclusion policy). Open Source Control panel, click the "Generate Commit Message" sparkle button. Request fails immediately; no commit message is generated. Expected behavior A commit message is generated from the staged/unstaged diff. Actual behavior Every request fails with a 422. Relevant log lines from GitHub Copilot Chat output channel: [error] Server error: 422 Unprocessable Entity ccreq:.copilotmd | promptFiltered | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | ~600-1000ms | [gitCommitMessageGenerator] Every failed request is tagged promptFiltered alongside the 422, suggesting the request is being rejected by a content filter or SKU-entitlement check on the backend before generation completes, rather than a genuine client-side prompt issue. Additional notes Confirmed not repo-specific: reproduces identically in a throwaway blank local repo unrelated to any GitHub org. Confirmed not an entitlement UI issue: github.com/settings/copilot shows "Copilot-generated commit messages" as Enabled. Suspect this is tied to backend handling of the free_educational_quota SKU against the gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 model specifically for this feature. title: macOS: VS Code 1.131 blocks Local Network access for integrated terminal/Remote-SSH (regression, works on 1.130)
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.131.0
- OS Version: macOS (darwin arm64) —macOS 26.6 (25G72)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. On macOS, with an app-level "Local Network" permission previously granted to VS Code, open the integrated terminal or use Remote-SSH to connect to a device on the local LAN (e.g. `192.168.1.x`).
2. Observe that any network call to a local/private IP fails at the OS level — e.g. `ping 192.168.1.2` inside the VS Code integrated terminal returns `ping: sendto: No route to host`, and `ssh 192.168.1.2` returns `ssh: connect to host 192.168.1.2 port 22: No route to host`.
3. Run the identical command (`ping 192.168.1.2` or `ssh 192.168.1.2`) in Terminal.app (or iTerm) on the same machine, same network — it succeeds immediately.
4. Confirm this is scoped to VS Code's process tree, not general connectivity or SSH config, since ping (a non-SSH, non-auth-dependent command) fails identically.
5. Downgrade to VS Code 1.130 — same commands, same machine, same network — LAN access works correctly in both the integrated terminal and via Remote-SSH.

Additional context:
- `System Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network` shows VS Code's toggle in an ambiguous/inconsistent state; toggling off/on and relaunching does not resolve the issue on 1.131.
- `tccutil reset LocalNetwork com.microsoft.VSCode` (and `tccutil reset LocalNetwork` system-wide) fail to reset the permission, including when run with `sudo` and from Recovery Mode.
- Remote-SSH log shows the failure occurring at the OS routing layer before any SSH handshake begins:
  `ssh: connect to host 192.168.1.2 port 22: No route to host`
- Suspect a regression in 1.131 related to how the app's Local Network TCC entitlement/entry is being requested or retained, causing macOS to silently deny LAN traffic from VS Code's spawned child processes (integrated terminal shell, Remote-SSH's ssh subprocess) even when the toggle appears enabled.
- Workaround: rolling back to 1.130 restores normal LAN access without any permission changes.

title: VS Code windows can get stuck with a black screen if 2 simultaneous "new chat response" messages occur
body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: ? (I don't think extensions can cause this issue) Version: 1.133.0-insider (user setup) Commit: 780ea331b2861816fe6bb8215d812933c81df83b Date: 2026-08-06T02:53:01Z Electron: 42.8.0 ElectronBuildId: 14845705 Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 Node.js: 24.18.0 V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0 @github/copilot: 1.0.78 @github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.9-preview.3 OS: 780ea331b2861816fe6bb8215d812933c81df83b Steps to Reproduce: UPDATE: These repro steps are out-of-date: see the response below for the updated repro steps. 1. Open 30 VS Code instances with 30 worktrees of some large repo with 30 agents running (you can have Copilot write a script to generate the worktrees) with 128 GB of RAM. With WSL (in a Dev Box). title: macOS: update restart hangs indefinitely in uv__threadpool_cleanup
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested. The hang begins after every extension host has exited normally.

- VS Code Version: 1.133.0-insider, commit 780ea331b2861816fe6bb8215d812933c81df83b
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2, arm64
- Electron Version: 42.8.0
- Chrome Version: 148.0.7778.280

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Leave VS Code Insiders running until an update has downloaded and is ready.
2. Trigger the update restart.
3. Observe that all windows close and extension hosts exit, but the main Code - Insiders process remains alive indefinitely and the updater cannot install the staged build.

This reproduced on two consecutive daily updates using the same installed build. A force quit allows the updater to continue. The staged build in the second occurrence also contains Electron 42.8.0.

### Native stack findings

A macOS spindump and a separate live 10-second sample show the same stable main-thread stack for every sample:

```text
CrBrowserMain
  exit
    __cxa_finalize_ranges
      uv__threadpool_cleanup
        uv_thread_join
          _pthread_join
            __ulock_wait
```

The main thread is waiting for the only remaining libuv worker, which remains blocked for every sample:

```text
libuv-worker
  _pthread_cond_wait
    __psynch_cvwait
```

All extension hosts exited with code 0 before the main process entered this state. No child processes remain attached to the main process. CPU usage is effectively zero.

The observed behavior is consistent with the libuv thread-pool exit-message relay failing to wake its final worker: other workers exit, while `uv__threadpool_cleanup` waits indefinitely to join the last worker. This looks like an Electron/libuv process-teardown issue rather than an extension-host shutdown veto.

No diagnostic files are attached, but additional sanitized stack details can be provided if needed.
