title: Simple file dialog: clicking a child of / updates the path but does not refresh the folder contents (regression in 1.133.0)
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (regression; 1.132.1 works)
- OS Version: Windows + WSL2 (Linux 6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2)
- Remote: WSL (remote server build a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open a folder in a WSL remote window.
2. File → Open File… (the simple file dialog is used for remote paths).
3. Navigate to the root folder `/`.
4. Click any child entry (e.g. `usr`, `etc`).

### Expected

The dialog navigates into the clicked folder and lists its contents.

### Actual

The path in the input box updates correctly to the clicked child, but the
listing is **not** refreshed — it keeps showing the contents of `/`. As a
result it is impossible to browse anywhere from `/` by clicking.

### Notes that narrow it down

- **Only `/` is affected.** From any other directory, clicking a child
  navigates and refreshes normally.
- **Not related to entry count** — `/` has ~25 entries.
- **Typing or pasting a full path + Enter works**, and browsing behaves
  normally from that point on — until returning to `/`, where the problem
  reappears.
- `/` itself lists correctly, so reading the directory succeeds. Only the
  refresh after selecting a child fails.

This suggests the contents-refresh is skipped when navigating *away from* `/`
— possibly a path-comparison/change-detection guard that mis-handles the root
path (e.g. after normalizing a trailing separator).

### Regression

- 1.132.1 — works
- 1.133.0 — broken

Possibly related to the simple file dialog changes around #319564 / #320385,
which involved the same list-repopulation behaviour.

title: Sessions are filtered out of the list in a remote window: working directories are compared without unwrapping their agent-host URIs
body:
### Summary

In a remote window (a dev container, here) agent sessions are filtered out of the sessions list because their working directories are reported as the remote's own `file:` URIs, while the workspace folder of such a window is a `vscode-remote:` URI. The containment check that decides list membership compares scheme first, so it can never match, however identical the paths are.

This is not a subset of sessions: in the `listSessions` payloads the agent host emitted in one log directory, **all 97 distinct sessions report `file:///workspace/printstream`, and none reports the `vscode-remote:` form**. So the list is empty in that window.

### Repro

1. Open a folder in a dev container.
2. Have agent sessions whose working directory is that folder.
3. Open the sessions list.

Observed: the sessions do not appear.

Expected: sessions on this workspace folder appear.

### Cause

List membership is decided by `_isSessionInWorkspace` → `_matchesAnyFolder` ([agentHostSessionListStore.ts:395-399](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionListStore.ts#L395-L399)):

```ts
private _matchesAnyFolder(workingDirectories: readonly URI[], folders: readonly IWorkspaceFolder[]): boolean {
	return workingDirectories.some(directory =>
		folders.some(folder => extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqualOrParent(directory, folder.uri))
	);
}
```

`isEqualOrParent` gates on the scheme before it compares anything else ([resources.ts:171-176](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/common/resources.ts#L171-L176)):

```ts
isEqualOrParent(base: URI, parentCandidate: URI, ignoreFragment: boolean = false): boolean {
	if (base.scheme === parentCandidate.scheme) {
		...
	}
```

so a `file:` working directory against a `vscode-remote:` folder short-circuits to `false`.

Running that matcher against the two forms this host actually emits, with the real folder URI of the window:

```js
const folder   = URI.parse('vscode-remote://dev-container%2B7b22…/workspace/printstream');
const wdRemote = URI.parse('vscode-remote://dev-container%2B7b22…/workspace/printstream');
const wdFile   = URI.parse('file:///workspace/printstream');

extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqualOrParent(wdRemote, folder)  // true  -> would list
extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqualOrParent(wdFile,   folder)  // false -> filtered out
wdFile.path === folder.path                                   // true  -> only the namespace differs
```

### Both forms come from the same host

The session-list summaries carry the `file:` form:

```json
{"resource":"claude:/83d5b222-…","provider":"claude","title":"Grouped toasts for print jobs",
 "workingDirectories":["file:///workspace/printstream"]}
```

An opened session's state carries the `vscode-remote:` form instead — and mixes the two inside one payload, since `project.uri` stays `file:`:

```json
{"project":{"uri":"file:///workspace/printstream","displayName":"printstream"},
 "workingDirectories":["vscode-remote://dev-container%2B7b22…/workspace/printstream"]}
```

I have not established why the two paths differ, and I would rather report that than guess. The candidates I can see are that the URI recorded depends on how the session was created (one started from the workbench in a remote window is handed the `vscode-remote:` URI, one started inside the container records its own `file:` path), or that a translation is applied on the state path but not on the list path. Either way, the path that decides visibility is the one receiving untranslated URIs.

### Notes on fixing

I am not opening a PR with this, because the remedies I can see are design calls rather than something to guess at:

- normalize working directories into the client's namespace before they reach the list, keeping the comparison a strict URI containment check; or
- make the list comparison namespace-aware for remote windows.

Comparing on path alone does make the sessions appear, but I would not propose it: two different remotes exposing the same path would then compare equal.

### Environment

VS Code 1.133.0 (`a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`), Windows client, dev container remote, Claude provider, single-folder window.

*AI disclosure: this issue was written with the assistance of AI.*

title: "View comments" tool doesn't reliably detect comments
body: Common experience- the button/banner to check the review comments did not show up on https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330982, when it did have comments. I manually told the agent to check the comments, and it used the View Comments tool, but the tool returned that there were no comments. A minute later, it did successfully detect that there were comments, and I was able to click the button. I suspect that we just don't check this very often, but when the tool is run, we should specifically try to refresh the state of the PR to see whether there are comments on it instead of relying on a cached value.

title: Editor patch tool bypasses agent sandbox write allowlist
body:
### Summary
A Copilot agent session whose sandbox policy allowed writes only to the workspace and system temp directory successfully wrote a file directly into the user’s home directory using the editor-level patch tool.

### Sandbox policy
- **Workspace:** `D:\Dev\.github-private`
- **Allowed read/write paths:**
  - `D:\Dev\.github-private`
  - `C:\Users\haral\AppData\Local\Temp`
- **Denied paths:** none explicitly listed
- **Network:** outbound blocked

### Reproduction
1. Start an agent session in `D:\Dev\.github-private`.
2. Confirm the effective sandbox policy has the two read/write paths above.
3. Ask the agent to create a simple “hello world” file in the user home directory.
4. The agent invokes the editor patch tool with an absolute path:
   ```text
   C:\Users\haral\hello-world.txt
   ```
5. The tool reports success, and the file exists with the expected contents:
   ```text
   Hello, World!
   ```

### Expected behavior
All agent write mechanisms, including editor-integrated patch/edit tools, should enforce the same sandbox write allowlist. An attempt to write `C:\Users\haral\hello-world.txt` should be rejected.

### Actual behavior
The patch tool created the file outside the permitted paths, suggesting editor-level file operations are not subject to the same write restrictions as sandboxed shell commands.

### Impact
An agent can modify arbitrary user-writable files outside the workspace despite an effective sandbox policy intended to restrict writes to the workspace and temp directory.

title: HTML language service does not report unmatched or invalid closing tags
body:
# HTML language service does not report unmatched or invalid closing tags Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **Yes** * VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (System setup) * OS Version: Windows 11 25H2 ### Steps to Reproduce: 1. Create a new `.html` file. 2. Add the following markup: ```html id="e9qzv7"
  • Services
    • Ship agency
    • Ship management
    • Consulation
    • Technical management
    • Bunker supply
    • Ship Chartering & brokering
    • Ship supply
    • ``` 3. Open the **Problems** panel. ### Actual Behavior No diagnostic is reported for the malformed HTML structure. There are at least two obvious structural errors: 1. `` is an unexpected/unmatched closing tag: ```html id="4prz7k" Services ^^^^ ``` 2. The closing `` tag incorrectly contains an attribute: ```html id="qg1h8j" ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ``` The Problems panel remains empty for these errors when using VS Code's built-in HTML language support. ### Expected Behavior The built-in HTML language service should report diagnostics for basic malformed HTML structure, including: * unexpected/unmatched closing tags; * mismatched opening and closing tags; * invalid attributes on closing tags. For example, an unexpected `` should be reported as an error or warning at the location of the invalid closing tag. ### Additional Information The issue reproduces with **all extensions disabled**, so this does not appear to be caused by an extension. I am not requesting full W3C/WHATWG validation here. The request is specifically for basic structural HTML diagnostics. A third-party HTML linter such as HTMLHint is currently required to catch some of these issues, while VS Code's built-in HTML language service does not report them. It would be useful if the built-in HTML language service could provide diagnostics for these basic structural errors directly in the **Problems** panel.

title: Copilot read_file truncation can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs and poison a chat session
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.61.0
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0
- OS Version: Windows
- Feature: Agent mode
- Selected model: GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: filtered synthetic excerpt in the attached clean-reproduction ZIP; identifiers removed

## Summary

The built-in Copilot `read_file` tool truncates lines with JavaScript `slice(0, 2000)`. If an astral Unicode character crosses that UTF-16 boundary, the tool result retains only the high surrogate. The malformed result is persisted in the chat session and included in subsequent requests. Both WebSocket and fallback HTTP then fail with `400 invalid_request_body`, and Retry cannot recover because it resends the same poisoned context.

The source appears to be:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/readFileTool.tsx

```ts
const MAX_LINE_LENGTH = 2000;

let contents = rawContents.split('\n').map(line => {
    if (line.length > MAX_LINE_LENGTH) {
        hadLongLines = true;
        return line.slice(0, MAX_LINE_LENGTH) + ' [truncated]';
    }
    return line;
}).join('\n');
```

## Minimal reproduction

The string operation itself is deterministic:

```js
const max = 2000;
const line = 'x'.repeat(max - 1) + '\u{1F6E1}' + 'tail';
const result = line.slice(0, max) + ' [truncated]';

console.log(JSON.stringify(result));
// Ends with: ...xxxxxxxx\ud83d [truncated]"
```

End-to-end reproduction using the attached `clean-repro` folder:

1. Run `node .\generate-repro-fixture.mjs` to create a valid UTF-8 fixture containing 1,999 ASCII characters, then `U+1F6E1`, then an ASCII tail.
2. Open the folder in a new VS Code window and start a fresh GPT-5.6 Sol agent chat.
3. Prompt: `This is a synthetic Unicode regression test. Use only read_file to read surrogate-boundary.txt from line 1 through line 1. Do not use terminal or other tools. After reading it, reply exactly FIRST_TURN_COMPLETE.`
4. Observe that the initial model step succeeds and invokes only `read_file`.
5. Observe that the immediate continuation fails with WebSocket `invalid_json`, a successful CAPI connectivity ping, and fallback HTTP `400 invalid_request_body`. The requested response is never emitted.

No second user prompt is needed; the failure occurs within this first turn when the model continues after the tool result.

## Actual result

The synthetic fixture is valid UTF-8 and contains no unpaired surrogates. Its `U+1F6E1` occupies UTF-16 indexes 1,999 and 2,000. The fresh chat ledger is valid JSON syntax but its persisted `read_file` result contains exactly one unpaired `U+D83D` at zero-based index 1,999, immediately followed by ` [truncated]`.

Representative extension-host log sequence:

```text
WebSocket CAPI error: [invalid_json] Invalid websocket message: failed to parse JSON value
CAPI ping successful, proceeding with chat request retry
Server error: 400 {"error":{"message":"Invalid body: failed to parse JSON value...","code":"invalid_request_body"}}
[ToolCallingLoop] Auto-retrying on error (attempt 1/3)
```

The attached `vscode-readfile-surrogate-clean-repro-20260814.zip` contains only public-safe synthetic evidence:

- `README.md`: reproduction instructions and exact prompt.
- `generate-repro-fixture.mjs`: deterministic fixture generator.
- `surrogate-boundary.txt`: generated valid UTF-8 fixture.
- `synthetic-extension.log`: filtered extension-host sequence with request IDs and UUIDs redacted.
- `session-structure.json`: content-blind structural scan proving `read_file` was the only tool and locating the lone surrogate.
- `extract-sanitized-log.ps1`: the exact event filter and redaction script.

The raw chat ledger and raw extension-host log are intentionally not attached.

## Expected result

- `read_file` truncation never splits a surrogate pair.
- Persisted tool results and outbound request bodies contain valid Unicode.
- Deterministic `400 invalid_request_body` errors are not retried multiple times with an unchanged body.
- If legacy persisted state contains an unpaired surrogate, Copilot either repairs it with `U+FFFD` or identifies the bad session and offers a clear recovery path.

## Proposed root fix

Before slicing at `MAX_LINE_LENGTH`, move the end index back by one when the boundary falls between a high and low surrogate. Add a unit test whose emoji begins at index 1,999.

This preserves the existing 2,000 UTF-16-unit cap while ensuring the result is well formed.

## Fix validation

Validated against the exact `@vscode/copilot-api` 0.5.2 lock:

- the focused regression test fails before the production fix and all 35 focused tests pass after it;
- typecheck and compile pass;
- the full Copilot unit suite passes (8,915 tests, with 129 skipped);
- the patched extension completes the synthetic GPT-5.6 Sol turn with `FIRST_TURN_COMPLETE`;
- a content-blind scan finds one `read_file` marker, no malformed JSON lines, no unpaired surrogates, and no WebSocket/JSON/400/retry failure signatures.

An exact cause-focused metadata search of `microsoft/vscode` issues was repeated on 2026-08-14. No issue title or exact query matched `read_file` splitting a surrogate pair, persisting an unpaired surrogate, or causing the resulting JSON failures. The broader results included #253136, a generic Copilot request-failure tracker, and #321578, titled "read_file reads only 2000 characters"; neither metadata result describes this surrogate-boundary corruption.

## Related but distinct prior art

https://github.com/github/copilot-sdk/pull/2283 repairs unpaired UTF-16 surrogate escapes in incoming Rust JSON-RPC frames. That is the same failure class but a different boundary. This issue is produced locally by VS Code's `read_file` line truncation and later fails on outbound CAPI request construction/parsing.

A defense-in-depth outbound/session sanitizer would be useful, but it should accompany rather than replace the producer fix.

title: Custom agent `agents:` frontmatter allowlist is parsed but never enforced by RunSubagentTool — coordinator can invoke any enabled agent, not just the ones listed
body:
## Requirements
 
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.48.1
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0-insider (commit 57bd491152b02dbf860469e75271c8e65c583ca9, 2026-08-14)
- OS Version: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26200 Build 26200
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent mode, custom agent with `agents:` frontmatter delegating via the `agent` tool (`runSubagent`)
- Selected model: Local/BYOK model (Qwen 3.8-27B) — noted for completeness, but the underlying issue is in `runSubagent`'s dispatch logic and isn't model-specific

## Summary

A custom agent's `agents:` frontmatter field is documented as an allowlist restricting which subagents a coordinator can delegate to (see [vscode-docs/docs/agents/subagents.md](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-docs/blob/main/docs/agents/subagents.md): "You can restrict which custom agents can be used as subagents by specifying the `agents` property in the main agent's frontmatter, and providing a list of allowed custom agents.").

In practice, the allowlist is parsed but never checked before dispatch. A coordinator agent with `agents: ['A', 'B']` can still successfully invoke any other enabled, non-`disable-model-invocation` custom agent in the workspace by name — the `agents:` list has no effect on what `runSubagent` will actually execute.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed in the wild with a real orchestrator agent, then isolated to a minimal case below.

**As observed:** A coordinator agent (`agents: ["Test Case", "Executor", "Plan"]` in frontmatter, body text referring to delegating to a "TDD"/"Test Case" subagent for Phase 1) was given a task and, unprompted, opened a subagent step labeled "Orchestrator: Research Tuff codebase" — invoking something outside its own `agents:` list before Phase 1 even began. See attached screenshot (`orchestrator-research-screenshot.png`): the response reads "I'll start by understanding the Tuff codebase and how this test case fits in, then run the orchestrator phases. Let me first research the project," followed by a collapsed subagent invocation titled "Orchestrator: Research Tuff codebase." No agent named "Research" (or anything matching that label) appears anywhere in the coordinator's `agents:` allowlist.

**Minimal isolation (not yet independently re-verified — please confirm on your end before triaging further):**

1. Create a coordinator agent, e.g. `.github/agents/coordinator.agent.md`:
   ```yaml
   ---
   name: Coordinator
   tools: ['agent']
   agents: ['Allowed']
   ---
   You orchestrate work. You must only ever delegate to the Allowed agent.
   ```
2. Create two more agents in the same folder:
   - `.github/agents/allowed.agent.md` with `name: Allowed`
   - `.github/agents/forbidden.agent.md` with `name: Forbidden` (no `disable-model-invocation`, so it remains available as a subagent by default)
3. In chat, select the Coordinator agent and send a prompt that explicitly asks it to invoke the Forbidden agent, e.g.: `Use the runSubagent tool to invoke the agent named "Forbidden" and ask it to say hello.`
4. Observe that the `runSubagent` tool call succeeds and Forbidden actually runs, despite not being present in Coordinator's `agents: ['Allowed']` list.

## Expected Behavior

`runSubagent` should reject (or the model should be prevented from even attempting) delegation to any custom agent not present in the calling agent's `agents:` list, matching the documented allowlist behavior.

## Actual Behavior

`runSubagent` dispatches to any enabled custom agent found by name, regardless of the calling agent's `agents:` list.

## Root Cause (source reference)

Looked through `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/tools/builtinTools/runSubagentTool.ts` on `main`:

- `IChatRequestModeInstructions` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatModel.ts`) has a field `readonly allowedSubagents?: readonly string[]` that appears to exist specifically for this purpose.
- `chatInputPart.ts` populates it once, from `mode.agents?.get()`, when a mode is selected at the top level of the chat input.
- However, in `RunSubagentTool.invoke()`, the name lookup goes straight to:
  ```ts
  private async getSubAgentByName(name: string): Promise<ICustomAgent | undefined> {
      const agents = await this.promptsService.getCustomAgents(CancellationToken.None);
      return agents.find(agent => agent.name === name && agent.enabled);
  }
  ```
  This searches every registered custom agent in the workspace by name and `enabled` status only — it never consults `currentModeInstructions.allowedSubagents` (or the equivalent `agents:` list) before returning a match.
- When building `modeInstructions` for the newly-dispatched subagent, `allowedSubagents` is explicitly discarded:
  ```ts
  modeInstructions = instructions && {
      name: subAgentName,
      content: instructions.content,
      toolReferences: this.languageModelToolsService.toToolReferences(instructions.toolReferences),
      allowedSubagents: undefined, // always undefined here
      metadata: instructions.metadata,
      isBuiltin: isBuiltinAgent(subagent.source, subagent.uri, this.productService),
  };
  ```
- Searching the whole file, `currentModeInstructions?.allowedSubagents` (or any equivalent check against the calling agent's own `agents:` list) is never read anywhere in `invoke()` or `prepareToolInvocation()` before a subagent is actually dispatched. The only place `allowedSubagents` is written is `chatInputPart.ts`; the only places it's set are the two spots above (one from `mode.agents`, one hardcoded `undefined`) — there is no read site that gates dispatch.

Net effect: the `agents:` field currently functions as documentation/UI hinting only, not as an enforced security or scoping boundary.

## Why this matters

Multi-agent orchestration patterns rely on this allowlist to keep a coordinator from silently substituting an unintended agent when names or descriptions are similar — the docs call this out directly as the reason the field exists. Right now that protection doesn't fire, so a coordinator can (and in my testing, did) invoke an agent outside its stated `agents:` list without any error, warning, or indication that the allowlist was bypassed.

## Suggested fix direction

In `RunSubagentTool.invoke()` (and ideally `prepareToolInvocation()` so it can fail fast / show a clear tool-prep error), before calling `getSubAgentByName`, check the requested `subAgentName` against `currentModeInstructions?.allowedSubagents` when that list is defined and non-empty, and reject with a clear error (similar to the existing "Requested agent '...' not found" error) if the name isn't present. Separately, `allowedSubagents: undefined` on the newly constructed `modeInstructions` for the dispatched subagent should presumably be populated from that subagent's own `agents:` frontmatter (`subagent.agents`), so nested delegation continues to respect each agent's own allowlist rather than losing it on every hop.

title: Copilot agent request can hang when WebSocket emits `error` without `close`
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.61.0
- VS Code Version: 1.133.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 Enterprise, build 26200
- Feature: Agent mode
- Selected model: Not captured in the sanitized occurrence record
- Logs: Sanitized signature and state transition below; no prompts or responses included

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long-running Copilot agent request using a model whose metadata enables the Responses API WebSocket endpoint.
2. While an active request is awaiting `handle.firstEvent` / `handle.done`, cause the Electron WebSocket to emit an `error` event without a subsequent `close` event. The linked PR's unit test reproduces this deterministically with `FakeWebSocket.simulateError()` and no close.
3. Observe that the agent remains pending until the user presses Stop or Retry.

## Expected

An active-socket error should settle the request immediately. The existing request-error path can then retry over HTTP when eligible, or show a terminal error to the user.

## Actual

`ChatWebSocketConnection` records the error in `_pendingErrorMessage`, but only calls `handleConnectionClose` from the socket `close` listener. If no close event follows, both `firstEvent` and `done` remain pending, so the request has no terminal transition and HTTP fallback never starts.

Observed log signature:

```text
[ChatWebSocketManager] Error for conversation <conversation-id> turn <request-id>: :
```

No matching later line was present for the same conversation and turn:

```text
[ChatWebSocketManager] Connection closed for conversation <conversation-id> turn <request-id> ...
```

After manual intervention, persisted state showed:

```text
native status: idle (1)
lastResponseState: 2
transport failure: chat-websocket-error
```

This occurred in five conversations in one extension host on the same day. One affected conversation reproduced the signature again while the investigation was running. Tool executions had completed; the silent interval began after a tool/sub-turn, not inside a terminal command.

## Root Cause

In `extensions/copilot/src/platform/networking/node/chatWebSocketManager.ts`, the active-socket `error` handler only stores `_pendingErrorMessage`. Request settlement occurs in the independent `close` handler. The implementation assumes every error is followed by close, which is not guaranteed by the observed Electron transport behavior.

## Proposed Fix

On an active-socket error:

1. Mark the connection closed.
2. Clear the active request from the connection.
3. Settle it through `handleConnectionClose(1006, '', errorMessage)`.
4. Close the underlying socket.

The linked PR's regression emits `error` without `close` and verifies `firstEvent` and `done` reject and the connection closes.

## Validation

- Test-only patch at `2e0b8aad459cc615790f9510ea8fe480ae034333`: the new regression timed out after 5000 ms, confirming that the request remained pending.
- Implementation patch applied: all 24 tests in `chatWebSocketManager.spec.ts` passed.
- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm run lint`: passed with zero warnings.
- TypeScript language diagnostics and `git diff --check`: clean.

Potentially related but not duplicate: #314336 and #329550. Neither public report identifies the error-without-close state-machine path.

The editor Chat panel then requests unrelated copilotcli session IDs that do not exist on the backend and displays: Session not found on backend: copilotcli:/ The standalone Agent window remains attached to the session that the editor Chat panel destroyed and hangs indefinitely. ## Environment - VS Code: 1.133.0 stable, User Installer, x64 - GitHub Copilot Chat: built-in version 0.61.0 - OS: Windows - Copilot account authenticated successfully - Dart and Flutter extensions disabled during reproduction ## Reproduction 1. title: Flexible Context Window & Custom Thinking Effort for BYOK
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

*Additional part of #325237*

Add these 2 new features for Custom Endpoint:

1. Add flexible context window.

Add `availableContextWindow`:

```jsonc
{
    "id": "custom",
    // ...
    "maxInputTokens": 1024000,
    "maxOutputTokens": 64000, // `maxTokens` - `maxInputTokens` or 16k if not defined
    "maxTokens": 1024000,
    "availableContextWindow": [200000, 500000, 1000000] // Use the smallest CWS by default to reduce token consumption.
}
```
> [!NOTE]
> When both `availableContextWindow` and `maxInputTokens`/`maxTokens` are defined, use the former first.

2. Add custom thinking effort.

Add `effort`:

```jsonc
{
    "id": "custom",
    // ...
    "efforts": ["off", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", "minimal"]
    // Display name: Off, Low, Medium, High, **Extra High**, Max, Minimal (usually for Gemini). Other efforts will be shown as-is.
    "defaultEffort": "medium" // Default: Closest to `medium`. It cannot be `max`.
    "useLegacyThinking": false // For older models which do not support efforts. Conflicts with `efforts` and `defaultEffort`.
}
```

3. Automatically save user's configuration of the settings above, except Max Effort.

title: New UI: Uneven padding around panel title tabs
body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.133.0 - OS Version: macOS 15.7.2 ### Description There is a noticeable UI inconsistency between the top Editor Tabs and the bottom Panel Tabs (e.g., Problems, Terminal) regarding container padding and hover boundaries. 1. **Uneven Container Padding (Panel Tabs only):** - **Editor Tabs:** The outer padding is uniform (`padding-top` matches `padding-left`). - **Panel Tabs:** The `padding-top` is visibly larger than the `padding-left`, resulting in an asymmetrical gap against the outer container. 2. **Inconsistent Hover Bounding Box:** - **Panel Tabs:** The hover highlight/border aligns precisely with the active click boundary. - **Editor Tabs:** The hover state expands beyond the active tab bounding box, rendering larger than the actual tab fill. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open any file in the editor and open the bottom panel. 2. Compare the outer container insets of the top Editor tab against the bottom Panel tab. 3. Hover over an inactive Editor tab versus an inactive Panel tab and compare the highlight boundaries against their active state bounds. ### Expected Behavior - Panel tabs should share the same balanced, symmetrical padding (`padding-top` == `padding-left`) as editor tabs. - Hover bounding boxes should behave consistently across both editor and panel tab bars. ### Actual Behavior - Panel tabs have asymmetrical outer insets (shorter top padding). - Editor tab hover states render with larger bounding boxes than their active click bounds, whereas panel tab hover states match strictly.

title: Built-in SQL language mode is displayed as "MS SQL", even though it's generic and dialect-agnostic
body:
## Description

VS Code's built-in "SQL Language Basics" extension (`vscode.sql`) registers the `sql` language ID with the display name **"MS SQL"**. This is misleading: the grammar is purely generic syntax highlighting (keywords, brackets), with no connection to Microsoft SQL Server / T-SQL specifically. It's applied by default to *every* `.sql` file, regardless of actual dialect.

I ran into this while editing PostgreSQL migration files — the status bar and language-mode picker both show "MS SQL" for a file that uses plain PostgreSQL syntax (`jsonb`, `->>`, `generated always as (...) stored`), none of which are T-SQL constructs. This is confusing: it strongly implies the file is being treated as, or should be treated as, Microsoft SQL Server syntax, when in fact the language mode does nothing dialect-specific at all.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ensure no SQL-dialect-specific extensions (e.g. `mssql`, `SQLTools`) are installed — only the built-in "SQL Language Basics".
2. Create a `.sql` file containing PostgreSQL-only syntax, e.g.:
   ```sql
   create table example (
     data jsonb,
     valid boolean generated always as (
       (data->>'valid')::boolean
     ) stored
   );
   ```
3. Open the file in VS Code.
4. Look at the language mode indicator in the bottom-right status bar, or open the language picker (click the indicator, or "Select Language Mode").

## Expected

The status bar / language picker shows a name that reflects the generic, dialect-agnostic nature of the built-in grammar — e.g. "SQL".

## Actual

It shows "MS SQL", despite the file containing no Microsoft SQL Server-specific syntax, and despite no mssql-related extension being installed. Confirmed via the extension's own "Feature Contributions" tab: ID: sql, Name: MS SQL, File Extensions: .sql, .dsql.

## Suggested fix

Rename the built-in sql language's display name from "MS SQL" to "SQL", to match its actual (generic) behavior.

## Details

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes — the built-in "SQL Language Basics" extension is itself the source, and is not affected by "disable all extensions" / --disable-extensions, since it's a built-in, not a marketplace extension.

title: Allow configuring the window zoom increment/step
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
It would be useful to have a setting to control the increment used by the **Zoom In** / **Zoom Out** commands (`Ctrl++` / `Ctrl+-`).

Currently, each step changes the zoom by 20%, which can feel too large, especially when working across monitors with different sizes or resolutions. While `window.zoomLevel` supports fractional values, these finer adjustments cannot be conveniently made with the keyboard shortcuts.

For example, a setting such as:

```json
"window.zoomStep": 0.25
```

could allow users to choose a finer zoom increment while keeping the existing value as the default.

title: Agent Host stops detached shells when idle sessions are released
body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Reproduction

This reproduces on macOS with a Copilot CLI session running through Agent Host. The detached command must run longer than the Agent Host idle-release grace period (currently 30 seconds).

1. Open VS Code Insiders and open a folder in an Agent Host-backed Copilot CLI chat session.
2. Send this prompt to the agent:

   ```text
   Use the bash tool with mode `async`, `detach: true`, and `initial_wait: 30` to run this command:

   node -e "setTimeout(() => require('fs').writeFileSync('/tmp/vscode-agent-host-detached-shell-repro', 'done'), 120000)"

   After the tool reports that the command started in the detached background, end the turn immediately. Do not call read_bash or wait for the command.
   ```

3. Confirm that the shell tool reports something similar to:

   ```text
   <command started in detached background with shellId: ...>
   ```

4. Wait for the chat session to become idle.
5. Navigate to another chat/session or close the chat so that the original session no longer has a subscribed client.
6. After navigating away, wait 130 seconds without reopening the session. This gives Agent Host time to release the idle session and gives the detached command time to finish if it survived.
7. Check whether the marker file was created:

   ```bash
   cat /tmp/vscode-agent-host-detached-shell-repro
   ```

8. Reopen the original chat and check for the detached-shell completion notification.

## Expected behavior

The AHP turn and session may become idle, but the detached shell continues running independently. Agent Host must not release/disconnect the provider session while the SDK still reports a running detached shell. After approximately two minutes:

- `/tmp/vscode-agent-host-detached-shell-repro` contains `done`;
- the session receives the detached-shell completion notification; and
- the agent can retrieve the completed shell output.

## Actual behavior

After the session becomes idle and loses its last subscriber, Agent Host releases the session after the grace period. Releasing the Copilot SDK session destroys the outstanding detached shell. The marker file is never created and no completion notification arrives.

The initial `session.idle` event is expected for detached work: detached shells are not part of the active agent loop. The bug is treating agent-loop idleness as sufficient to release the provider session.

## Lifecycle evidence

In the original report:

1. Two commands started with `mode: async` and `detach: true`.
2. Both tool calls completed immediately with detached shell IDs.
3. The SDK emitted `session.idle`, and AHP correctly completed the active turn.
4. One detached shell completed before eviction, proving that detached work survives the initial idle transition.
5. The other shell was still running when the final client unsubscribed.
6. Agent Host logged `Evicting idle session` and `Releasing idle session from memory`.
7. The SDK emitted `session.shutdown` and destroyed the session.
8. The remaining detached shell never emitted `shell_detached_completed`.

The SDK exposes authoritative detached-task state through `session.rpc.tasks.refresh()` and `session.rpc.tasks.list()`. A running detached shell is represented as a shell task with `attachmentMode: detached` and status `running` or `idle`.

## Proposed behavior / fix

Before idle eviction tears down provider resources, ask the provider whether each chat can release its in-memory backing. For Copilot, refresh/list SDK tasks and defer release while a detached shell is still running. Keep AHP state idle; only provider eviction is deferred. Retry release after the normal grace period.

Draft fix: [#330132](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330132)

(Written by Copilot)

title: Disable the pet’s peeking animation
body:
### Problem

The VS Code pet repeatedly peeks up and down over the chat input bar. The amount of motion is distracting while I am doing other work on the screen.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Show the VS Code pet above the chat input bar.
2. Leave it in the state where it peeks up and down.
3. Work elsewhere on the screen.

### Actual behavior

The pet continues peeking up and down, creating persistent motion that draws attention away from other work.

### Expected behavior

Provide a way to reduce or disable this motion, or keep the pet still, so it is not distracting.

title: Automations should not rename themselves
body:
Now that the automations view is using the session flat list, the name of the run is no longer controlled by the view. Agents typically name their session as they start a turn, so either we need some alternate way to correlate an automation with its run, or we should prevent agents from renaming a session when it detects its an automation.

When automations moves to the agent host there should be a flag that the agent host can check for when considering a rename. Until then, we may need some other fix around this.

## AI investigation

The current behavior spans two naming paths:

- [`AutomationRunner`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/browser/automationRunner.ts) starts the background request with `title: automation.name`, then persists the returned session resource on the automation run.
- [`AutomationHistorySection`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/automationsView.ts) resolves each run to an `ISession` and passes those sessions to `SessionsFlatList`.
- [`SessionsFlatList` / `SessionItemRenderer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views/sessionsList.ts) renders the session's observable title. As a result, a later agent-driven chat rename becomes the visible run name instead of the automation name.

There is already an `ISession.isAutomation` observable, but for local Agent Host sessions it is currently populated by [`LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts) by matching session resources against persisted automation runs. That happens in the browser after the run has been linked to its created session, so it is not available early enough to suppress first-turn renaming inside Agent Host.

The Agent Host decision points are [`AgentHostSessionTitleController.seedTitleFromFirstMessage`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostSessionTitleController.ts) and `prepareInstructionForAgent`. The latter supplies the `rename_chat` reminder when active-agent title generation is enabled. Once automations are owned by Agent Host, an automation flag on `SessionState` could be checked at those points before seeding a title or asking the agent to rename the chat.

Until that flag exists in Agent Host, possible short-term options are:

1. Keep the history row correlated with its automation by having the Automations view provide the automation name when rendering the linked session.
2. Propagate an automation marker during programmatic session creation through [`ISessionsManagementService`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/browser/sessionsManagementService.ts) into Agent Host session state, then check it in the title controller.

title: Agent file tools incorrectly prompt "Allow reading file outside of workspace?" for the current workspace in WSL
body:
### Description

When a Copilot agent uses a file-search or file-reading tool against the current workspace while in WSL, VS Code prompts:

> Allow reading file outside of workspace?

The requested directory is the active workspace itself, not a path outside it.

This occurred both when the tool explicitly supplied the workspace's absolute path and when the tool omitted the path and relied on its current-working-directory default.

I used `--disable-extensions .` to disable all extensions (except WSL, which is enabled automatically) and it occurs the same way.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a WSL folder as the workspace in VS Code Insiders. For example, open a terminal at a dir like this:

   `/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace`

   And run `code-insiders .`.

2. Start a Copilot agent chat by asking it to do some ordinary modification.
3. See the agent invoke a glob/file-search operation with:

   ```json
   {
     "pattern": "**/*",
     "paths": "/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace"
   }
   ```

4. Observe the "Allow reading file outside of workspace?" prompt.

If you then get Copilot to invoke the same tool without an explicit path, the same outside-of-workspace prompt appears again.

```json
{
  "pattern": "**/*"
}
```

### Expected behavior

File operations whose resolved target is inside the active workspace should not trigger the outside-of-workspace permission prompt.

Omitting the path should use the agent's workspace working directory and should likewise not be classified as external access.

### Actual behavior

VS Code presents the outside-of-workspace permission prompt for both:

- An explicit absolute path exactly equal to the active workspace root.
- A glob operation with no path argument, which defaults to the agent's current working directory.

The second dialog displays the workspace name (`copilot-confused-workspace`) as the target even though the tool input contains only:

```json
{
  "pattern": "**/*"
}
```

### Verification that the path is inside the workspace

The agent process reported:

```text
$ pwd
/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace

$ readlink -f .
/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace

$ readlink -f /home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace
/home/dagood/try/copilot-confused-workspace
```

The current directory and requested directory resolve to exactly the same path. There is no symlink mismatch or other filesystem anomaly.

### Environment

- Remote environment: WSL2, Ubuntu 26.04

title: Electron 42.8.1 regresses Windows renderer layout and startup performance
body:
## Summary

Electron 42.8.1 introduces a Windows renderer layout regression that materially slows VS Code startup. The regression remains in Electron 42.9.3.

The same VS Code application on Electron 42.8.1 is 50-87 ms slower than on 42.8.0 in repeated startup measurements. A minimal renderer benchmark isolates the change to forced Blink layout: 110.0 ms on 42.8.0 versus 145.2 ms on 42.8.1 (+32%). Equivalent JavaScript execution does not regress.

![Electron 42.8.1 Windows renderer layout regression](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a47a044f-ec49-4f69-a6d3-b4fc92dadae0)

## Impact on VS Code startup

This was found while analyzing Windows desktop startup performance across 154 published Insiders builds from July 1 through August 18.

Adjacent published build boundary:

| | Last known good | First known bad |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Commit | `f844934f854c9277a48627aac77ebcea69591ae1` | `68939d5cba5de82713a8b1bd8e34a10b44d465d5` |
| VS Code version | 1.134.0-insider | 1.134.0-insider |
| Electron | 42.8.0 | 42.8.1 |
| Chromium | 148.0.7778.271 | 148.0.7778.280 |
| V8 | 14.8.178.33-electron.0 | 14.8.178.38-electron.0 |
| Node.js | 24.17.0 | 24.18.1 |
| Median startup | 1364 ms | 1411 ms |

Measured regression:

- +47 ms (+3.45%)
- Bootstrap 95% interval: +36 ms to +61 ms
- The next published build remains at the first-bad level: -5 ms, interval -19 ms to +4 ms.

The source range contains `1fc102e9ae7264920fcc41986d7c4d8231f557f7`, `chore: bump electron@42.8.1` (#330244).

## Runtime/app partition

Reciprocal hybrid builds separate the runtime and VS Code application:

| Electron runtime | VS Code app | Median startup |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 42.8.0 | Last-good app | 1374 ms (A1), 1362 ms (A2) |
| 42.8.1 | Last-good app | 1419 ms |
| 42.8.0 | First-bad app | 1425 ms |
| 42.8.1 | First-bad app | 1425 ms |

The runtime-only hybrid reproduces a 45-57 ms increase. Product changes in the same published-build gap add overlapping critical-path cost, but do not explain the Electron-only result.

## Official Electron runtime comparison

The identical last-good VS Code app was grafted onto verified official Windows x64 Electron archives:

| Runtime | Median startup |
| --- | ---: |
| Electron 42.8.0 A1 | 1372 ms |
| Electron 42.8.1 | 1459 ms |
| Electron 42.9.3 | 1494 ms |
| Electron 42.8.0 A2 | 1409 ms |

Comparisons:

- 42.8.1 versus 42.8.0 A1: +87 ms (+6.34%), interval +75 ms to +111 ms
- 42.8.1 versus 42.8.0 A2: +50 ms (+3.55%), interval +28 ms to +73 ms
- 42.8.0 control drift: +37 ms, interval +28 ms to +58 ms
- 42.9.3 versus 42.8.1: +35 ms, comparable to control drift; 42.9.3 does not recover

Each batch used three warmups and fifteen measured starts. Execution was interleaved 42.8.0 / 42.8.1 / 42.9.3 / 42.8.0.

## Trace results

Trace categories:

```text
base,browser,content,loading,navigation,mojom,renderer_host,renderer,startup,toplevel,v8,blink,blink.user_timing,gpu,cc,disabled-by-default-v8.compile,disabled-by-default-v8.cpu_profiler,disabled-by-default-devtools.timeline,devtools.timeline
```

Two marked Chrome JSON startup traces per adjacent build were captured. Instrumented median:

- Renderer start to workbench ready: 1933.2 ms -> 2041.5 ms (+108.2 ms)

Largest renderer changes:

| Trace event | 42.8.0 | 42.8.1 | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `RunTask` | 1481.1 ms | 1596.5 ms | +115.4 ms |
| `Receive mojo message` | 892.7 ms | 981.8 ms | +89.0 ms |
| Style/layout update | 158.3 ms | 192.9 ms | +34.7 ms |
| `UpdateLayoutTree` | 51.9 ms | 76.0 ms | +24.1 ms |
| `V8.CompileCode` | 462.6 ms | 486.3 ms | +23.7 ms |

Browser-process `RunTask` changes by only +5.2 ms. The regression is renderer-specific.

The VS Code `perfBaseline` worker moves from approximately 20 ms to 24 ms. Running the same Fibonacci computation under Electron-as-Node is instead 2.5% faster on 42.8.1, which further narrows the regression to the renderer rather than generic Node/V8 execution.

## Minimal renderer reproduction

A fresh hidden renderer performs:

1. Recursive Fibonacci computation
2. Dynamic function compilation
3. Creation of 1,000 inline elements
4. Forty alternating class changes followed by `offsetWidth` reads
5. Repeated warm Fibonacci computation

Median of 15 alternating runs:

| Electron | Cold JS | Compile | Forced layout | Warm JS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 42.8.0 | 1.2 ms | 11.7 ms | 110.0 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.8.1 | 1.2 ms | 12.6 ms | 145.2 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.9.3 | 1.1 ms | 12.8 ms | 143.5 ms | 6.5 ms |

The forced-layout workload is 32% slower beginning in 42.8.1 and remains regressed in 42.9.3. Cold and warm JavaScript are effectively unchanged.

Core workload:

```js
for (let index = 0; index < 1000; index++) {
	const element = document.createElement('span');
	element.textContent = `item-${index}`;
	target.appendChild(element);
}

const start = performance.now();
for (let index = 0; index < 40; index++) {
	target.className = index % 2 === 0 ? 'compact' : 'expanded';
	width += target.offsetWidth;
}
const duration = performance.now() - start;
```

## Upstream change suspects

Electron 42.8.1 includes:

- Node.js 24.18.1
- Chromium/V8 patch updates
- Updated PGO profiles, including `win-x64.pgo.txt`

Electron 42.9.0 updates PGO profiles again, but 42.9.3 remains regressed in the minimal forced-layout benchmark.

Release references:

- https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v42.8.1
- https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/tag/v42.9.3

## Host and scenario

- Windows x64, OS build 10.0.26200
- AMD EPYC 7763, 32 logical processors
- High performance power plan
- 128 GB RAM
- Official VS Code Insiders ZIP archives, SHA-256 verified
- Standard startup: deterministic local folder and one text file
- Extensions, updates, experiments, workspace trust, GPU, telemetry, and crash reporting disabled
- Primary statistic: median warm startup

VS Code arguments include:

```text
--skip-welcome
--skip-release-notes
--disable-updates
--disable-experiments
--disable-extensions
--disable-workspace-trust
--disable-gpu
--disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion
--disable-telemetry
--disable-crash-reporter
```

## Traces

GitHub's issue attachment endpoint rejected both ZIP and JSON content types, so the raw traces could not be attached directly. They are retained locally and can be shared through an approved artifact channel:

| Trace | Size | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Electron 42.8.0 good JSON trace | 100.67 MB | `CDD566E02D1EC87D8C7F5FEE251DB824880E1347F9415C447E073FA944A588D6` |
| Electron 42.8.1 bad JSON trace | 100.98 MB | `F101DCE0EDC32BD6C229F284B65D0A417CD2F3F46E84E75AA8F6E3F4AE61BB04` |

Compressed copies are 9.84 MB and 9.82 MB respectively.

## Mitigation

#331670 coalesces one repeated VS Code forced-layout hotspot and conservatively recovers 5-14 ms, but it does not address the underlying Electron/Blink regression.

## Expected

Electron patch updates should not make the same Windows renderer forced-layout workload approximately 32% slower or add 50+ ms to VS Code startup with an identical application.

title: VS Code Chat automatically includes entire (HUGE) terminal output in model context without explicit user consent
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version:
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0
- OS Version: Ubuntu 26.04 (WSL 2 on Windows 11)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): auto
- Logs: (contains sensitive data, will not send)

## Description

When starting a chat using the built-in VS Code Chat extension, VS Code automatically includes context from the IDE, including information from open terminal sessions.

In my case, the context included the **entire output of a long-running terminal session**, including the command that was executed and all of its accumulated output. This happened without any explicit indication that the terminal contents were going to be included in the request, or an opportunity to review or exclude that content before it was sent to the model.

I only discovered this because, after several turns in one of the sessions, the automatically selected model (Sonnet) eventually failed with:

> `model_max_prompt_tokens_exceeded`

I then investigated the requests and found that the automatically generated context for the initial chat message already exceeded **500,000 input tokens**.

Importantly, this was **not isolated to a single session or model**. I observed the same behavior across multiple chat sessions under the same circumstances, regardless of which model was selected. The excessive context was already being provided by the VS Code Chat harness **before the model's first turn**; it was not generated or requested by the model itself.

The terminal in question was running a Spring Boot application in debug mode and had accumulated a very large amount of output. As a result, the automatically generated context included hundreds of thousands of tokens of terminal content.

My actual prompt was very short and specific, referring to code in a particular file. None of the terminal output was relevant to the question, yet it was nevertheless included in the model context.

This is particularly concerning from a privacy and security perspective. Terminal output can contain information that users reasonably expect to remain local, including:

* Environment/configuration information
* Internal URLs and hostnames
* Identifiers and tokens
* Application data
* Stack traces and request data
* Other sensitive information produced by development tools

I would expect context providers such as terminal sessions to either:

1. Include only a small, relevant portion of terminal output by default (for example, the most recent N lines), or
2. Require explicit user selection/consent before sending potentially large terminal contents to a model, and
3. Clearly indicate in the Chat UI what terminal content is being included in the request.

At minimum, automatically including an entire terminal buffer—especially one that can grow to hundreds of thousands of tokens—seems problematic both in terms of **privacy** and **resource/token usage**.

### Expected behavior

When terminal content is automatically added to Chat context, VS Code should limit the amount of content included and/or provide a clear indication and an opportunity for the user to review or remove it before the request is sent.

### Actual behavior

The entire accumulated output of an open terminal session was automatically included in the initial model request, resulting in more than 500k input tokens of context despite the user's prompt being unrelated to the terminal output.

The behavior was reproducible across multiple sessions and models under the same circumstances, and the excessive context was present before the model's first turn.

### Steps to Reproduce:

1. Have a terminal session with a very long ouput from the last command (or a running command)
2. Prompt anything in a new chat session
3. Observe the input tokens sent using the Agent Debug Logs feature

title: Remote AHP host custom agent is unavailable at session creation and cannot remain selected
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Bundled with VS Code 1.134 client; remote Copilot CLI runtime 1.0.79-6
- VS Code Version: 1.134 client; remote standalone Agent Host 1.133.0 Stable (`a5b500951314efd502d07465bd138dfbd714a960`)
- OS Version: macOS 26 on Apple Silicon (client); Windows 11 (remote host)
- Feature: Agents window connected to a remote standalone Agent Host over an AHP tunnel
- Selected model: GPT-5.6 Sol, xhigh
- AHP version: 0.8

## Description

A user-level custom agent installed on a remote AHP host (`~/.copilot/agents/*.agent.md`) is discovered by the host and works when selected directly through AHP, but the VS Code Agents window cannot use it correctly.

This is specific to a custom agent supplied by a remote AHP host, not a workspace custom agent disappearing after the first prompt.

There are three related symptoms:

1. **The host custom agent is missing when creating a session.** In the new-session UI for the AHP tunnel, the Agent picker does not list the custom agent, so the session cannot be started with it.
2. **It appears after the session starts, but cannot be selected.** Once a default Copilot session exists, the custom agent appears under the Agent button. Clicking it does not change the active selection; the button remains on the default `Agent`.
3. **A direct AHP selection works for one turn, but the UI does not retain it.** Sending `chat/turnStarted` with the discovered custom agent's `message.agent.uri` runs that turn with the custom agent. After the turn completes and the session is viewed or continued in VS Code, the UI does not stay on that custom agent. The next UI-submitted message runs as the default assistant.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a standalone Agent Host on a remote machine and connect VS Code to it through an AHP tunnel.
2. Put a valid user-level custom agent on the host under `~/.copilot/agents/<name>.agent.md`.
3. In the macOS VS Code Agents window, start creating a new session on that AHP host.
4. Open the Agent picker.
5. Observe that the host custom agent is not available before session creation.
6. Start the session with the default Copilot agent.
7. Open the Agent picker in the running session.
8. Observe that the host custom agent is now listed.
9. Click the custom agent.
10. Observe that the active selection remains `Agent`; submitting a message uses the default assistant.
11. As a control, create/subscribe to a session over AHP and send the first `chat/turnStarted` with `message.agent.uri` set to the URI advertised for the host custom agent.
12. Observe that this turn correctly uses the custom agent.
13. Continue the same session from the VS Code Agents window.
14. Observe that the custom-agent selection is not retained and the next turn uses the default assistant.

## Diagnostic evidence

The host advertises the custom agent in the materialized session's `customizations`, with a file URI under the remote host's `~/.copilot/agents` directory. Direct AHP invocation using that URI succeeds, proving that the file is valid, discovered, and usable by the provider.

For the direct-AHP turn, the session records a successful custom-agent selection and follows its instructions. Before the next message submitted through the VS Code UI, the session records the equivalent of:

```text
custom agent selected
custom agent deselected
user message submitted
response uses default assistant
```

The selected model remains unchanged, and no selection error is shown to the user.

## Expected behavior

- Host-scoped custom agents should be available in the Agent picker while creating a session on that AHP host.
- Clicking a host custom agent in a running session should update the active Agent selection.
- After a custom agent is selected, the Agents window should retain that choice for subsequent messages (and after reopening the session) until the user explicitly selects another agent.
- UI-submitted turns should include the selected custom agent's `message.agent.uri`.

## Actual behavior

- The host custom agent is absent during new-session creation.
- It becomes visible only after a default session exists.
- Clicking it does not activate it.
- A direct AHP-selected custom agent works for one turn, but VS Code clears/omits the selection on the next UI turn without warning.

title: fix: handle snippy post-insertion rejection to avoid unhandled error (fixes #331807)
body:
### Summary The Copilot code-referencing ("snippy") post-insertion check is fired as an unawaited, uncaught floating promise from `NextEditProvider.runSnippy`. When the snippy service returns a non-200 response, `SnippyFetchService.fetch` throws, `handlePostInsertion` re-throws, and — because the promise is neither awaited nor given a rejection handler — the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection that is reported to error telemetry. The specific 400 seen here (`source too short (must be at least 110 tokens, but is 105)`) is an expected server-side rejection: the client's local pre-check uses a 65-lexeme minimum while the service enforces its own, higher token minimum, so short accepted suggestions routinely trip it. Impact is noisy telemetry only — no user-facing functionality breaks. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#331807 Recommended reviewer: `@ulugbekna` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | `333d9a4053e` (vendored-import boundary) | | Author | `@not-determined` | | PR | n/a | | Message | Initial import of the Copilot Chat extension ("Hello Copilot") | | Why | The fire-and-forget `handlePostInsertion(...)` call in `runSnippy` has existed without a rejection handler since the extension was vendored into `microsoft/vscode`. `git blame` shows the throwing call site predates all recent changes, so this is a **pre-existing** bug re-bucketed by telemetry (the specific 400 message text changed the bucket), not a new regression. | > Pre-existing / re-bucketing: the underlying floating-promise pattern is not introduced by any recent commit in the regression window; the new bucket is driven by the server's error-message text, not by a change in triggering logic. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User accepts NES participant NEP as NextEditProvider.runSnippy participant Svc as SnippyService.handlePostInsertion participant Fetch as SnippyFetchService.fetch participant Server as Snippy service User->>NEP: handleAcceptance() Note over NEP: ⚠️ Root cause:
handlePostInsertion() called
without await / .catch NEP->>Svc: handlePostInsertion(uri, doc, edit) Svc->>Fetch: fetchMatch(source) Fetch->>Server: POST snippy/match Server-->>Fetch: 400 "source too short (110 > 105)" Note over Fetch: 💥 throw new Error(`Failed with status 400 ...`) Fetch-->>Svc: rejects Svc-->>NEP: rejects (floating promise) Note over NEP: Unhandled rejection → error telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditProvider.ts` | root cause / fix site | L1648-1653: `this._snippyService.handlePostInsertion(...)` called with no `await` and no `.catch`, so a rejection escapes as an unhandled error | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyServiceImpl.ts` | rethrow site | L40-44: `catch (e) { throw e; }` re-throws the fetch failure up to the floating caller | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyFetcher.ts` | crash site | L70-71: `if (fetchResponse.status !== 200) { throw new Error(\`Failed with status \$\{status} ...\`); }` | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyCompute.ts` | contributing mismatch | L8: `MinTokenLength = 65` — client pre-check floor is looser than the service's 110-token floor, so short sources pass the client gate but are rejected by the server | ### Repro Steps 1. Use the Copilot Chat extension with Next Edit Suggestions (code referencing / public-code matching enabled). 2. Accept a short next-edit suggestion whose surrounding source clears the client's local 65-lexeme pre-check but is below the snippy service's token minimum (~110 tokens). 3. `runSnippy` fires `handlePostInsertion`; the snippy `/match` request returns HTTP 400 (`source too short`). 4. Because the promise is unawaited and uncaught, the rejection surfaces as an unhandled error and is reported to telemetry. Deterministic given a source between the two thresholds; otherwise triggered whenever the service rejects the request for any reason. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`nextEditProvider.ts`): `runSnippy` now `await`s `handlePostInsertion(...)` inside a `try/catch` and routes any failure to `this._logService.error(e, ...)`. This attaches a rejection handler at the fire-and-forget boundary that owns the background operation, so the failure is recorded as a *handled* error through the existing log/telemetry pipeline instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection. This follows the principle of fixing the error at the boundary that owns the best-effort background work — snippy code-referencing is explicitly a best-effort check, so its failures should not appear as unhandled application errors. The `logService.error` call preserves telemetry visibility of genuine failures; nothing is silently swallowed. **Alternatives considered:** - Aligning the client `MinTokenLength` (65) with the server's 110-token floor — rejected: the exact server threshold is not a stable contract the client can safely hardcode, other non-200 responses would still leak, and it would not fix the underlying missing-rejection-handler defect. - Swallowing the error inside `snippyServiceImpl.handlePostInsertion` (removing the rethrow) — rejected: that hides all fetch failures from callers/telemetry rather than handling them at the fire-and-forget site, and would violate the "never silence errors" principle by dropping them entirely. ### Recommended Owner `@ulugbekna` — dominant recent author of `nextEditProvider.ts` (author of the most recent NES/inline-edits commits touching this file, merged into `microsoft/vscode`), making them the natural owner for this fire-and-forget call site in the inline-edits area. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/32384235362) · opus48 · 461.5 AIC · ⌖ 11.7 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests) --- > [!NOTE] > This was originally intended as a pull request, but PR creation failed. The changes have been pushed to the branch [`fix/snippy-post-insertion-unhandled-rejection-aa290b8d76b80828`](https://github.com/vscodebot-pr/vscode/tree/fix/snippy-post-insertion-unhandled-rejection-aa290b8d76b80828). > > **Original error:** ERR_API: [2026-08-20T15:39:49.753Z] create pull request in microsoft/vscode failed (attempt 1) Original error: Validation Failed: {"resource":"PullRequest","code":"custom","field":"fork_collab","message":"fork_collab Fork collab can't be granted by someone without permission"} - https://docs.github.com/rest/pulls/pulls#create-a-pull-request Retryable: false Suggestion: This error cannot be resolved by retrying. title: Agent Host session restore is canceled by no-op proxy configuration restart
body:
## Summary

After quitting and restarting VS Code Insiders, the previously open Agents Window session can display a persistent:

> Couldn't open session
>
> Canceled

The session still exists and is healthy. A retry moments later restores the same session with its complete history, but the initial transient failure has already been rendered into the chat model and remains visible.

## Specific user impact

On every affected restart, the user's previously active agent session appears unrecoverable even though no session data was lost. The restored editor is left on a blocking error instead of the conversation, so the user cannot immediately continue where they left off and may reasonably believe that the session and its work have been lost. Recovery depends on triggering another subscription, such as navigating away from the session and back, rather than happening automatically.

## Reproduction

1. Open an existing Copilot Agent Host session in the Agents Window.
2. Quit VS Code.
3. Start VS Code and allow the previous window/session state to restore.
4. Observe that the restored session can show `Couldn't open session / Canceled`.
5. Navigate away and back, or otherwise cause a fresh subscription.
6. The same session loads successfully with its prior turns.

## Correlated timeline

From an Agent Host debug bundle captured on 2026-08-20:

- `08:23:27.947`: the window subscribes to the restored session, its default chat, and annotations.
- `08:23:27.948`: startup configuration synchronization sends the proxy settings. Both `http.proxy` and `http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal` are empty strings.
- `08:23:29.137`: the initial Copilot client starts successfully.
- `08:23:31.842`: Agent Host logs `Restarting CopilotClient (CAPI proxy configuration changed ((none) -> (none)))`.
- `08:23:33.320`: Copilot chat discovery completes successfully: 4,294 SDK sessions were enumerated and the affected session was already known to Agent Host.
- `08:23:34.244`: resuming the affected chat backing fails with `Canceled`.
- `08:23:34.245`–`08:23:34.294`: the session, chat, and annotations subscriptions fail with JSON-RPC `-32603`: `Failed to restore session ...: Canceled`.
- `08:23:34.259`: the client issues another session subscription.
- `08:23:35.481`: the replacement Copilot client starts successfully.
- `08:23:38.905`: the same chat backing resumes successfully.
- `08:23:41.477`: Agent Host restores the same session with all 27 turns.
- `08:23:41.480`: the retry subscription succeeds.

This confirms that the session is present and restorable. Its initial restore is canceled while the Copilot client is restarted.

## Likely root cause

The initial Copilot client records an absent Kerberos proxy SPN as `undefined`. The synchronized default for `http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal` is later received as `""`. In `CopilotAgent._refreshProxy()`, the strict comparison treats those two equivalent "no value" states as different:

```ts
const effectiveKerberosSpn = process.env['COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN'] || this._configurationService.getRootValue(...);
if (effectiveProxy === this._appliedProxy && effectiveKerberosSpn === this._appliedProxyKerberosSpn) {
	return;
}
```

The resulting restart is logged as `(none) -> (none)` because the message only includes the proxy URL, not the SPN difference. `_applyPendingClientRestart()` then clears the live SDK chat entries and stops the client while restoration is in progress, causing the resume operation to reject with `Canceled`.

The proxy-setting synchronization and Kerberos-SPN restart comparison were introduced in [#331488](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331488).

## Relationship to #331648

This is related to [#331648](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331648) in user-visible behavior, but it is a different host-side race:

- #331648 produced `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` because restore raced provider catalog migration.
- This occurrence produces JSON-RPC `-32603 / Canceled` after catalog discovery succeeds, because a no-op proxy configuration difference restarts the Copilot client during restore.
- The affected Insiders build already contains the fixes from [#331716](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331716) and [#331721](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331721).

Both failures become sticky because the workbench converts the first transient subscription failure into synthetic `Couldn't open session` chat history, even when a later subscription succeeds.

## Suggested fix

- Normalize empty proxy and Kerberos-SPN strings to `undefined` before storing and comparing effective values.
- Add a regression test proving that startup synchronization from an unset SPN to `""` does not restart the Copilot client.
- Consider making restoration resilient to unavoidable client restarts by delaying the restart while session restoration is active or retrying transient `Canceled` restore failures before rendering a permanent load error.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Copilot `fetch failed` to send `google` apikey and to download `claud SDK`
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 1.0.81-0
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0
- OS Version: WIN10 21H2
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Add Models in Langage Models, and Agent Host

  * Failed to download `claud SDK`:
    ```
    2026-08-19 22:57:24.445 [warning] [AgentService] initial provider catalog for claude was unavailable; retrying before listing sessions Provider claude cannot enumerate its native session catalog yet
    2026-08-19 22:57:24.446 [warning] [Claude] SDK unavailable while listing chats to migrate Failed to download claude SDK from https://main.vscode-cdn.net/agent-sdk/claude/0.3.220/win32-x64.tgz (cache target: C:\Users\user\AppData\Roaming\Code\agent-host\sdk-cache\claude\0.3.220\win32-x64).     2026-08-19 22:57:24.446 [error] [ProtocolServer] Request 'listSessions' failed Provider claude cannot enumerate its native session catalog yet
    ```

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Set `http.proxy` "socks5://....:.."
2. Add Models -> Select "google" -> Input apikey -> press enter -> "error" found
2. Happens to see the `Failed to download `claud SDK`` error in debug output `Agent Host`

Additional:
1. The openrouters one has no this issue from the begining.
2. If `http.proxy` was "http://....:.." then it fixs the "fetch failed `google` " issue. Not sure if it also fixs the "download `claud SDK`".

Therefore, the issue looks like to be: the adding "openrouters" and adding "google gemini" used different set of codes. The former one used vscode fetch, and the latter one used nodejs fetch which missed to support socks5 proxy.

title: fix: guard against parallel-refresh node removal in AsyncDataTree (fixes #331811)
body:
### Summary

The SCM History tree intermittently crashes with `TreeError [SCM History Tree] Unknown compressed tree node`, thrown from `CompressibleObjectTreeModel.setChildren` when it looks up a node that is no longer present in the inner compressed tree's node map. This is a lifecycle/race bug in the base `AsyncDataTree`: between the awaited `refreshNode(node)` and the synchronous `render(node)` in `refreshAndRenderNode`, a concurrent (parallel/re-entrant) refresh of an ancestor can splice `node` out of the inner tree, so the subsequent `render` dispatches `setChildren` for an element the inner model has already dropped. The bucket has hits across nearly all Insider versions (approximately 1.110 through 1.135), so it is a **pre-existing** race, not a 1.134 regression. The fix adds an early-return guard at the same orchestration point that already guards for disposal, skipping the stale render when the inner tree no longer contains the node.

Fixes microsoft/vscode\#331811
Recommended reviewer: `@benibenj`

### Culprit Commit

Not a single-commit regression. `get_bucket_history` for bucket `936d3c96-3e33-8eb3-8c5a-8ca47ff47cd1` shows hits in effectively every tracked Insider version going back to ~1.110 (April 2026), so the `recent-regression`/`stable-anomaly` labels reflect re-bucketing rather than a new defect. Culprit: **not identified — pre-existing race** in the base async tree refresh/render orchestration (`src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts`). The same class of inner-vs-outer node-map desync was previously addressed for a sibling code path in `c81880276af` ("fix: make AsyncDataTree.hasNode check inner tree consistency (fixes \#316443)").

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[updateChildren / parallel refresh scheduled] --> B[refreshAndRenderNode node]
    B --> C[await refreshNode node]
    C -. concurrent ancestor refresh .-> D[inner compressed tree splices node out]
    C --> E[render node]
    E --> F[tree.setChildren node, children]
    F --> G[CompressibleObjectTreeModel.setChildren]
    G --> H{nodes.get element}
    H -- undefined --> I[throw TreeError: Unknown compressed tree node]
    D --> H
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts` — `refreshAndRenderNode` orchestration point (the fix).
- `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/compressedObjectTreeModel.ts` — `setChildren` crash site (throws when `nodes.get(element)` is undefined); unchanged.
- `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/objectTree.ts` — `hasElement` consistency check used by the guard; unchanged.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmHistoryViewPane.ts` — consumer creating the "SCM History Tree" and driving throttled `updateChildren`; unchanged.

### Repro Steps

Non-deterministic (timing-dependent). It surfaces when the SCM History view issues overlapping/throttled refreshes (e.g. rapid repository/ref changes or graph reloads) such that an ancestor refresh removes a node from the inner compressed tree while a child's `refreshAndRenderNode` is between its awaited refresh and its synchronous render. Telemetry shows ~82 users / ~88 hits across many versions.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts`, `refreshAndRenderNode`: after the `await this.refreshNode(...)` resolves and after the existing disposal guard, add:

```typescript
if (node !== this.root && !this.tree.hasElement(node)) {
    return; // node removed from the inner tree by a parallel refresh (#331811)
}
```

This fixes the bug at the data producer / orchestration point — the exact place that decides whether to dispatch a render — rather than at the crash site inside the throwing utility. `this.tree.hasElement(node)` queries the inner compressed tree model's node map, which is the same map `setChildren` reads and throws on; if a concurrent refresh has already removed the node, we skip the now-stale render instead of asking the inner model to operate on an element it no longer knows about. It mirrors the two disposal guards already present in this method (`#228211`, `#199264`) and is consistent with the framework's own acknowledgement of this scenario in `_updateChildren`, which wraps a parallel-refresh `rerender` in try/catch noting "missing nodes are fine, this could've resulted from parallel refresh calls". The precedent commit `c81880276af` applied the identical inner-tree consistency check to `hasNode` for the sibling `isCollapsed` path.

After this change, `refreshAndRenderNode` cannot dispatch `render(node)` to `setChildren(node, ...)` for a node a concurrent refresh removed, because the render is now skipped whenever the inner tree no longer contains `node`.

**Alternatives considered**

- Wrapping `setChildren`/`render` in try/catch: rejected — hides the symptom at the crash site, swallows a real error, and would break telemetry, rather than preventing the stale render at its source.
- Guarding inside `CompressibleObjectTreeModel.setChildren`: rejected — that is the crash site in a shared low-level utility; absorbing a missing-node there masks other legitimate callers' contract violations instead of fixing the async-tree orchestration that produced the stale call.

### Recommended Owner

`@benibenj` — most active recent author of `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts` and the surrounding compressed-tree code (core VS Code team member, active within the last day). The precedent fix for the same inner/outer node-map desync class also lives in this area.
