title: Agents window does not restore completed remote AHP turn after laptop wake
body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in with VS Code 1.134
- VS Code Version: 1.134
- OS Version: Latest macOS
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window connected to a remote AHP host session
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Unknown / not model-specific
- Logs: Not captured

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a local macOS machine, open the VS Code Agents window and connect to a session hosted remotely through AHP.
2. Start a turn that performs an externally observable action. In my case, the turn removed an existing GitHub comment and created a new GitHub issue.
3. Close the laptop while the turn is running, interrupting the local client connection while leaving the remote AHP host/session running.
4. After the remote action has had time to complete, reopen the laptop and return to the session in the Agents window.
5. Try to get an update from the session.
6. Reload the Agents window.

## Expected

After reconnecting, the Agents window should reconcile the remote session state, mark the completed turn as finished, and display its response and tool results.

## Actual

The turn initially appears stuck in the Agents window and its completed response is not shown. However, the requested action did complete remotely: the original GitHub comment was gone and a new issue had been created. Once I reload the Agents window, the session history updates and shows the end of the latest turn.

This indicates that execution and persisted session history completed correctly on the remote AHP host, but the already-open local Agents window did not reconcile the terminal turn state/result after wake and reconnect. A full reload is required before the completed turn becomes visible.

This is specifically a local Agents window connected to a **remote AHP host session**, not a local Agent Host session.

Possibly related:

- #330888, which covers a resumed Agent Host session remaining in progress.
- #331310, which addresses completing the response for the turn that actually ended.

The distinguishing detail here is that the remote turn demonstrably completed and produced its external side effects while the laptop was closed, but the completed result was lost from the local UI after reconnect.

title: Code actions with `arguments` fail with "Actual command not found" when the Quick Fix menu is open for ~2s (regression in 1.134.0)
body: Type: Bug - VS Code Version: 1.134.0 (regression; 1.133.0 is unaffected) - OS Version: reproduced on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu - Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A — reproducing requires an extension that contributes a code action, but it is not specific to any one extension. ### Summary Since 1.134.0, activating a `CodeAction` whose `command` carries a non-empty `arguments` array fails with: ``` Actual command not found, wanted to execute / ``` ...if the Quick Fix / lightbulb menu has been open for roughly two seconds before the item is activated. Activating quickly (well under ~2s) still works, which makes this easy to miss. This affects any extension using this very common API shape. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Install/run an extension that contributes a code action whose command has arguments, e.g.: ```ts vscode.languages.registerCodeActionsProvider("*", { provideCodeActions(document, range) { const action = new vscode.CodeAction("Repro", vscode.CodeActionKind.QuickFix) action.command = { command: "repro.doThing", title: "Repro", arguments: [{ uri: document.uri.toString() }], // <-- non-empty arguments } return [action] }, }) ``` 2. Open the Quick Fix menu with Ctrl+. / Cmd+.. 3. Wait ~2 seconds. 4. Activate the item with Enter. **Expected:** the command runs with its arguments. **Actual:** nothing happens, and an error notification appears: `Actual command not found, wanted to execute repro.doThing /1`. Confirmed with no mouse interaction at all, so this is not a hover/focus artifact. ### Analysis When a code action's command carries `arguments`, `CommandsConverter#toInternal` (`src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostCommands.ts`) does not pass the command through as-is. It caches the real command plus arguments under a generated key (`` `${command} /${++cachIdPool}` ``), substitutes a delegating command, and registers deletion of that cache entry on a `DisposableStore` owned by the `CodeActionSet`. Since 1.134.0 that store is disposed while the lightbulb menu is still open, so by the time the user activates the item the cache entry is gone and the delegating command has nothing to resolve to. The likely trigger is #330142 ("fix: memory leak in code actions", merged 2026-08-13, shipped in 1.134.0), which touches `src/vs/editor/contrib/codeAction/browser/codeActionModel.ts`. From its own description: > `CodeActionModel.trigger()` permanently disposed its reusable `MutableDisposable` before the asynchronous `CodeActionSet` was assigned. The later assignment became a no-op, so closing the editor never disposed the set and its extension-host command payloads remained cached. That leak is precisely what previously kept the cached payload alive long enough for the user to click. Now the set is genuinely disposed — but apparently too eagerly, while the menu it belongs to is still on screen and actionable. The fix looks correct in intent; the lifetime just needs to extend until the menu is dismissed or the action is resolved. For what it's worth, I diffed the extension-host side across the two releases: `CommandsConverter#toInternal` and `releaseCodeActions` are byte-identical between 1.133.0 and 1.134.0 (only minifier renames differ), so the behavior change is entirely workbench-side. ### Impact Any user who opens the Quick Fix menu and hesitates a couple of seconds gets a silent no-op plus a confusing error notification. It is not specific to one extension — it hits every extension that passes `arguments` on a code action command. We hit this in Cline and worked around it locally by dropping `arguments` from our code action commands and recovering the context inside the handlers (cline/cline#13402), but the underlying bug affects the ecosystem broadly.

* OS Version: Windows 11
Version: 1.134.0 (user setup)
Date: 2026-08-18T18:24:44Z

@github/copilot: 1.0.81-0
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.11

## Steps to Reproduce:

1. Install Visual Studio Code on Windows.
2. Allow VS Code to automatically update to a newer version.
3. Monitor process execution during or immediately following the update.
4. Observe execution of the VS Code `code-tunnel.exe` component, located under the VS Code installation directory.
5. In my environment, the observed command line was:
   `code-tunnel.exe tunnel kill`
6. The execution is detected by endpoint security/MDR tooling as potential SSH/lateral-movement activity.

## What happened?

Each time VS Code updates, execution of `code-tunnel.exe` appears to trigger a security detection in our endpoint security environment.

The detection identifies the activity as related to VS Code Remote Tunnels and maps it to MITRE ATT&CK T1021.004 (SSH). The security tooling therefore generates an alert that requires investigation.

I do not believe this is necessarily a bug in VS Code, and I am not claiming that the behavior is malicious. I am reporting it because the behavior appears to occur as part of the normal VS Code update process and can cause security products to generate potentially misleading security alerts.

## Expected behavior

If `code-tunnel.exe tunnel kill` is expected behavior during a VS Code update, it would be helpful to document this behavior and/or consider whether the execution can be performed in a way that is less likely to be interpreted by endpoint security products as an unexpected remote-access operation.

If this behavior is not expected during a normal update, this report may help identify why `code-tunnel.exe` is being invoked.

## Additional information

The security detection is specifically associated with:

`code-tunnel.exe tunnel kill`

The security product identifies the activity as:

* MITRE ATT&CK Tactic: TA0008 — Lateral Movement
* MITRE ATT&CK Technique: T1021.004 — SSH

The security alert is generated even though the VS Code installation/update itself is legitimate.

I am primarily submitting this as an awareness/compatibility concern so the VS Code team can confirm whether this behavior is expected and, if so, whether there is anything that can be done to prevent legitimate VS Code updates from unnecessarily generating security alerts.

title: Add enterprise policies for dictation model and LLM cleanup
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

VS Code currently exposes the `DictationEnabled` enterprise policy for the `dictation.enabled` master switch. Add enterprise policies for the two settings that determine whether dictation data leaves the device:

- `dictation.model`: allow administrators to enforce the on-device transcription model and prevent selection of a cloud transcription backend.
- `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup`: allow administrators to disable language-model cleanup so transcript text is not sent to a Copilot model.

This should enable an enforceable configuration where dictation remains available, audio transcription runs on-device, and LLM transcript cleanup is disabled.

`dictation.showTranscript` is intentionally out of scope because it controls interim transcript visibility only and is not a data-egress boundary.

title: [regression] Paste in chat changed functionality; now unusable; regresses months of fixes
body: With a change in v1.134, now paste into chat changes functionality, breaking months of fixes, and is now unusable for original functionality. **Paste no longer "pastes", but forces the user into a "add clipboard as attachment".** This breaks expected paste semantics; if "paste as attachment" is desired (a reasonable separate functionality), it would be best to create a separate "paste as attachment" command. For months and months there have been many, many issues with paste. Originally paste-as-Markdown was turned on by default, which was great, but it was broken (see e.g. #319733). There were many issues in paste, but finally in #328212 @lramos15 did a commendable amount of work and in PR #328466 and PR #320984 fixed a lot of those bugs!! 🎉 Finally users were ready to simply copy and paste and get clean Markdown without cruft everywhere. Unfortunately v1.134 breaks `Ctrl+V` paste and turn it into something different: an "add clipboard as attachment" functionality. 1. Right-click on a previous prompt. 2. Select "Copy" to copy the previous prompt. 3. Use `Ctrl+V` to paste the previous prompt into the new-prompt field as Markdown. **Expected for `Ctrl+V`:** The clean Markdown is pasted, which @lramos15 worked so hard to fix in PR #320984 and PR #328466. **Actual:** A `attachment:Pasted text` is added to the chat. There is no way to edit it. It gets worse: 1. Right-click on a previous prompt. 2. Select "Copy" to copy the previous prompt. 3. Use `Ctrl+Shift+V` to paste the previous prompt into the new-prompt field as plain text. **Expected for `Ctrl+Shift+V`:** Plain text is pasted. **Actual:** A `attachment:Pasted text` is added to the chat, and it pastes the _Markdown_ — it would seem there is now no longer any way to choose between Markdown and plan text. "Add clipboard as attachment" is a completely separate semantic operation than "paste". It's fine to add that as a separate command if someone wants that. It would even be reasonable to decide to bind it a separate keystroke (configurable by the user). But plesae don't break the "paste" operation; that is a standard, decades-old convention when editing a text field. **Please bring back normal the "Paste as Markdown" functionality for `Ctrl+V`, and "Paste as Plain Text" for `Ctrl+Shift+V`. This new forced functionality does waste a significant amount of time. ``` Version: 1.134.0 (user setup) Commit: 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419 Date: 2026-08-18T18:24:44Z Electron: 42.8.1 ElectronBuildId: 14906494 Chromium: 148.0.7778.280 Node.js: 24.18.1 V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0 @github/copilot: 1.0.81-0 @github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.11 OS: 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419 ```

title: Unbounded concurrent reads in prompt discovery exhaust file handles (EMFILE) and hang the window
body: Type: Bug Prompt/agent/skill/hook discovery reads every visible customization file with an unbounded `Promise.all`. On profiles with a large number of agent-plugin, skill and extension-contributed customization files, a burst of discovery passes exhausts the process file handle limit and the window becomes unresponsive with `EMFILE: too many open files`. This is reproducible **with no folder open**, because the files involved are global (`~/.copilot`, `~/.claude`, `.vscode/extensions`, `settings.json`, `mcp.json`). ### Symptoms The main process reaches ~150k pending libuv filesystem requests and ~9.5k OS handles, after which unrelated reads fail: ``` [error] Unknown (FileSystemError): Error: EMFILE: too many open files, open 'c:\Users\\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\settings.json' [error] Unknown (FileSystemError): Error: EMFILE: too many open files, open 'c:\Users\\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\mcp.json' [error] [computeAgentDiscoveryInfo] Failed to parse agent file: .../azqr-cost-optimize.agent.md Error: EMFILE: too many open files [error] [computeSkillDiscoveryInfo] Failed to validate Agent skill file: .../SKILL.md Error: EMFILE: too many open files [error] ChatSessionStore: Error writing chat session Unable to write file '...chatSessions/.jsonl' (EMFILE: too many open files) [warning] No ptyHost heartbeat after 6 seconds [info] Extension host (LocalProcess pid: NNNNN) is unresponsive. ``` Once handles are exhausted the failure spreads well beyond chat: the terminal pty host misses heartbeats, chat sessions fail to persist, and extension hosts are marked unresponsive. ### Cause Three discovery paths in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts` fan out over every discovered file without a concurrency bound, and each iteration performs a `fileService.readFile` via `parseNew`: - `computeSlashCommandDiscoveryInfo` — `Promise.all(slashCommandFiles.map(...))` (prompts + skills) - `computeAgentDiscoveryInfo` — `Promise.all(allAgentFiles.map(...))` - `computeHooks` — `Promise.all(hookFiles.map(...))` Two properties turn this into handle exhaustion rather than a slow scan: 1. **No concurrency limit.** Every discovered file is opened at once. Note that `computeSkillDiscoveryInfo` and `getInstructionsDiscoveryInfo` in the same file already iterate sequentially, so the exposure is limited to the three sites above. 2. **Invalidation does not cancel in-flight work.** In `CachedPromise`, a change event clears the cached promise but leaves the running computation going: ```ts this._register(this.getEvent()(() => { this.cachedPromise = undefined; delayer.trigger(() => this.onDidUpdatePromiseEmitter.fire()); })); ``` The `Delayer` debounces the *notification*, not the recompute, so successive invalidations stack multiple full scans concurrently. The fan-out is easy to trigger because `ExtensionPromptFileService` invalidates **all** prompt types from a single context key change: ```ts this.contextKeyService.onDidChangeContext(e => { if (e.affectsSome(this._contributedWhenKeys)) { for (const type of ALL_PROMPT_TYPES) { this._onDidChange.fire({ type }); } } }); ``` So one setting change on an extension that contributes many `when`-gated customizations invalidates every type at once, and each type re-reads its full file set. In the profile that produced the logs above, the recursively scanned customization roots held **1,256 directories / 2,621 files** (735 `SKILL.md`, 34 agent files, 30 instruction files). Discovery costs several filesystem operations per file — `readSkills` performs a `pathExists` per candidate, a `resolve` per directory, and `isResolvedWithin` issues two `realpath` calls per skill in addition to the `readFile` — so one full pass is on the order of 10k operations, and the observed ~150k pending operations corresponds to roughly fifteen passes in flight simultaneously. ### Notes Bounded concurrency is already the established pattern elsewhere in the codebase — `Limiter` is used 35+ times under `src/vs/platform`, including for directly comparable discovery work (`agentService.ts` uses `new Limiter(4)` for session discovery). These three call sites simply don't use it. I've opened a PR that bounds the three unbounded sites with `Limiter`, which addresses the handle exhaustion. The non-cancelling invalidation in `CachedPromise` is left as a separate follow-up since it changes cancellation semantics and is better reviewed on its own. VS Code version: 1.134.0 (commit 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419) OS version: Windows 11

title: Power-save blocker does not cover custom LanguageModelChatProvider models
body:
The power-save blocker added for #276546 does not appear to cover Agent sessions that use models provided by third-party `LanguageModelChatProvider` extensions.

The implementation in commit `de441dc178462184fb8772bfff47d325f752bf3e` acquires the power-save blocker in `ChatMLFetcher`, i.e. around model requests made through Copilot's own fetch path.

However, when an Agent session uses a model registered by another extension through `LanguageModelChatProvider`, the model request is handled by that provider instead and does not pass through `ChatMLFetcher`.

As a result, the computer can still go to sleep while such an Agent session is actively working.

### Example

I am using a Codex model exposed to Copilot Chat through the third-party Universal Chat Provider extension.

The effective path is roughly:

```text
Copilot Agent
    ↓
VS Code LanguageModelChatProvider API
    ↓
third-party model provider
    ↓
Codex
```

An Agent task can be actively running through this provider, but Windows still goes to sleep according to the configured idle timeout.

### Expected behavior

The power-save blocker should ideally follow the **Agent execution lifecycle**, independent of which language-model provider is being used.

While at least one Agent session is actively working, VS Code should prevent automatic system sleep.

This should include activity such as:

```text
model request
→ tool call
→ terminal command
→ file operation
→ model request
→ tests/build
→ model request
```

The display should still be allowed to turn off normally.

Sleep inhibition should be released once the Agent session has:

* finished;
* been cancelled; or
* reached a state where it is waiting for user interaction.

### Why the Agent/session layer may be preferable

The current implementation is tied to individual model requests and keeps the blocker alive for a grace period after a request completes.

That works for many cases, but it has two limitations:

1. **Third-party model providers are not covered** if their requests bypass `ChatMLFetcher`.
2. **Long-running tool calls may outlive the grace period**, even though the Agent itself is still actively working.

For example:

```text
model response finishes
→ build/test command runs for several minutes
→ next model request
```

The Agent is active for the entire period, but a blocker attached only to model fetching cannot reliably represent that state.

Moving or additionally applying the power-save blocker at the Agent/session execution level would make the behavior provider-independent and would cover the complete Agent workflow.

### Multiple VS Code windows

This should also work when multiple VS Code windows are open.

If any window has an Agent session that is actively working, the system should remain awake. Normal sleep should resume only after there are no actively working Agent sessions in any window.

### Related

* #276546
* Commit: `de441dc178462184fb8772bfff47d325f752bf3e`

This is not intended to duplicate #276546, but to report a gap in its current implementation for custom language-model providers and for Agent activity occurring between model requests.

VS Code Version: 1.134.0
OS Version: Sonoma 14.0 (23A344)

When renaming a file or folder with a very long name in the VS Code Explorer sidebar, the inline rename input field does not automatically expand or offer horizontal scrolling. As a result, a significant portion of the filename remains invisible (either the beginning or the end is cut off), making it difficult to edit the full name properly.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open VS Code and navigate to the Explorer (file tree).
2. Create or select a file/folder with an intentionally long name (e.g., more than 40 characters).
3. Ensure that horizontal scrolling is enabled
4. Trigger the rename command on that item.

Actual result:

The input field shows only a portion of the full name. It does not scroll horizontally, nor does it expand to the full available width. The user cannot see the entire filename at once, which hampers editing.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e375387f-d782-461e-b438-b96aeeb390a7

Expected result:

Provide a horizontal scrollbar within the input field itself, so that the user can scroll to view and edit the entire filename comfortably.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0
- OS Version: Windows 11

# Description
This issue is regarding the newly introduced dictation function in VS Code. I have no specific steps on how to reproduce this unfortunately.

My company blocks automatic downloading of the Nemotron resulting in the following error message:
`Could not download the nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b speech-to-text model, which can happen on networks that block the model registry. You can install it from a downloaded package instead.`

The VS Code [website](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/configure/accessibility/voice#_install-the-model-from-a-local-package) mentions the following:
`If network restrictions prevent VS Code from downloading the on-device model, download the official CPU model package separately. Then run Chat: Install Dictation Model from Local Package... and select the ZIP file or prepared model folder.`

It is, however, not that trivial as to how to get this up and running manually. Maybe the documentation could be improved a bit in this regard. In any case, I'll describe how I got it to work eventually in case it is useful to others. I am not sure whether I have missed something completely that would simplify manual installation, but that would in any case then be useful to add to the documentation.

# Manual installation & issues
The first minor issue is that when browsing for the model, VS Code does not allow to select ".zip" files.

When searching for this model online, you'll only find the [Hugging Face repository](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b) of this model and the [NVIDIA webpage](https://build.nvidia.com/nvidia/nemotron-asr-streaming/modelcard), which refers to the same Hugging Face page. The problem is that the Hugging Face version of the model is not accepted by VS Code as it must be a specific ONNX version of the model. It was a bit difficult to find out how to obtain a suitable model. I now found a Microsoft [blogpost](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/foundry-local-v1-1/) on live transcriptions that provided some guidance.  The code I now use to download the model:
```python
"""
This script downloads a streaming speech model using Foundry Local.

Requirements:
    pip install foundry-local-sdk
"""

from pathlib import Path

from foundry_local_sdk import Configuration, FoundryLocalManager

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Initialize Foundry Local
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cache_dir = Path(".") / "nemotron"
config = Configuration(
    app_name="fetch-vscode-dictation-model",
    model_cache_dir=str(cache_dir),
)
FoundryLocalManager.initialize(config)
manager = FoundryLocalManager.instance

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Download and load the streaming speech model
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

model = manager.catalog.get_model("nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b")

if not model.is_cached:
    print("Downloading model...")
    model.download(lambda progress: print(f"\r  Progress: {progress:.1f}%", end="", flush=True))
    print("\n  Download complete.")

print(f"Model: {model.id}")
print(f"Prepared model folder: {model.get_path()}")
```

Selecting the cache directory of this model is accepted by VS Code and its files are saved to `%APPDATA%\Code\chatDictationModels\`. However, dictation still would not work as the same error message kept popping up. I found out that VS Code also needs a Foundry Local runtime that might be downloaded together with the model normally, which I cannot check myself. VS Code will, misleadingly, keep showing the error that the model must first be downloaded manually instead.

I now circumvented this by also downloading the runtime files manually here:
https://main.vscode-cdn.net/dictation-runtime/foundry-local/1.2.3/win32-x64.tgz
And extracting the files, such that:
```
%APPDATA%\Code\chatDictationRuntime\1.2.3\
├── .complete-win32-x64
├── prebuilds\win32-x64\foundry_local_napi.node
└── foundry-local-core\win32-x64\ (Foundry Local + onnxruntime DLLs)
```
Finally, the `.complete-win32-x64` file must be added manually to the directory above. It's contents must be set to `1.2.3`. After that, the dictation function started working for me.

title: Copilot chat text input - paste as markdown from m365 copilot includes css style
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

```
Version: 1.134.0 (user setup)
Commit: 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419
Date: 2026-08-18T18:24:44Z
Electron: 42.8.1
ElectronBuildId: 14906494
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.1
V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
@github/copilot: 1.0.81-0
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.11
OS: 110a328ea54b42367b803ec53ee0bf52ef26b419
```

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open https://m365.cloud.microsoft/ (m365 copilot subscription required)
2. Ask the agent to write some rich text
3. Copy the text
4. Paste into the Github Copilot Chat window
5. Select "paste as markdown" if prompted to select or if it attaches instead of pasting
6. Notice the content is proceeded by:
```
a {
    text-decoration: none;
    color: #464feb;
}
tr th, tr td {
    border: 1px solid #e6e6e6;
}
tr th {
    background-color: #f5f5f5;
}
```

Notes:
* pasting into https://www.slatejs.org/examples/paste-html seems to have the same result, leading me to think there is something weird about M365 Copilot's clipboard contents
* pasting into https://evercoder.github.io/clipboard-inspector/ reveals a completely different HTML with no css style but instead an embedded style attribute

title: Improved display of Hooks/Custom Agents/Skills/MCP Servers/Instructions
body: **Problems** There are a number of inconsistencies in how each of these are grouped/displayed 1. In some of them we have the folder name displayed, and not others 2. In some of them we have the file name dispalyed, and not others 3. The format for displaying folder/file names differ 4. Instructions have no notion of `Workspace` level instructions I suppose this makes sense as its a whole different type of customization, however I'd expect Skills to follow this style as skills too can be loaded based on location/on demand 5. When adding MCP servers we cannot select the folder in which the MCP server is added (all others support this, Agents, Skills, Instructions, Hooks) 6. There's a `Workspace` group for Agents, Skills, Hooks, MCP Servers, but no group by folder name 7. Quick picks for creating skills/agents differ based on where its invoked from (sometimes we start with workspace folder and in others we start with the sub directory like .claude, .github, etc) 8. When we have a quick pick for creating skills/agents etc, the quick pick can be quite large and would be nice to group the locations based on worksapce folder, (we kind of already do this for user folder) | | Folder Name Displayed | File Path Displayed | | ------------- |:-------------:| -----:| | Agents | No | No | | Skills | No | No | | Instructions | ✅ | ✅ | | Hooks | ✅ | ✅ | | MCP Servers | No | No | ### Agents ### Skills ### Create Skill Quickpick in Agents Window ### Create Skill Quickpick in Editor Window (Customization UI) ### Create Skill Quickpick in Editor Window (Command Palette) ## Instructions ### Create Instructions in Agents Window (Command Palette) ### Create Instructions in Editor Window (Customization UI) ### Create Instructions in Editor Window (Command Palette) ## Hooks ### MCP Servers

title: Extension activation telemetry's `codeLoadingTime` is misleading
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.134.0
- OS Version: Windows 11

The `codeLoadingTime` reported to telemetry for extension activation time can be misleading--it is essentially a wall-clock time measurement around module load. For CJS extensions, this is a good approximation--since `require()` will be synchronous--but for ESM extensions, this breaks down. With ESM, if any other extensions are activating or working hard at the same time (which is highly likely especially at startup), then any work they are doing could be counted against your extension's code loading time, as their async work is interleaved with the async work of loading your extension code.

The bottom line is that ESM extension code loading time could be severely overstated in telemetry.

Having a truly accurate measurement would probably involve complex `async_hooks` / `AsyncLocalStorage` stuff, but a cheap approximation could be achieved just by including, e.g., some measures for event loop utilization/delay to estimate the contention, along with telemetry readers focusing on code loading measurements without much contention--so they can get a more "fair" understanding.

title: Worker bootstrap blob URLs are never revoked (13 GB of blob_storage on my machine)
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.135.0-insider (0052619e71feb774a574b37f4f2ea20c36547373) and 1.129.0-insider (174edf23f6d4eaf609df4a4619a1c8b523939cfd)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), arm64

`blob_storage` in my Code - Insiders profile had grown to 13 GB. Tracing it back, `getWorkerBootstrapUrl` creates a blob URL for every web worker and nothing ever revokes it.

A registered blob URL holds a strong reference to its `Blob` until it is revoked or the document unloads. So every worker creation permanently retains its bootstrap script, which is currently around 1.1 MB because the bootstrap inlines the whole NLS message table and `product.json`.

`application.experimental.rendererProfiling` was enabled on my install by the startup experiment (my `settings.json` did not contain the setting), and `rendererAutoProfiler` builds up to three `CpuProfileAnalysisWorker`s per triggered session. Over a few days that came to roughly 12,800 retained blobs.

## Steps to Reproduce

You do not need a slow machine for this, since the long task can be forced.

1. Launch an isolated instance with no extensions:

   ```
   "/Applications/Visual Studio Code - Insiders.app/Contents/MacOS/Code - Insiders" \
     --user-data-dir=/tmp/vsc-repro --extensions-dir=/tmp/vsc-repro-ext \
     --remote-debugging-port=9333 --new-window
   ```

   (Keep that path short. The Electron IPC socket path is capped at 103 characters and a longer one fails with `EINVAL`.)

2. Set `"application.experimental.rendererProfiling": true` in that instance.

3. Open Help > Toggle Developer Tools and install a probe on the console:

   ```js
   const created = [], revoked = [];
   const c = URL.createObjectURL.bind(URL), r = URL.revokeObjectURL.bind(URL);
   URL.createObjectURL = function (o) { const u = c(o); created.push({ url: u, size: o.size }); return u; };
   URL.revokeObjectURL = function (u) { revoked.push(u); return r(u); };
   globalThis.__probe = { created, revoked };
   ```

4. Force a long task past the `perfBaseline * 10` threshold:

   ```js
   setTimeout(() => { const t0 = performance.now(); while (performance.now() - t0 < 3000) {} }, 0);
   ```

5. Wait about 20 seconds, then read the probe:

   ```js
   [globalThis.__probe.created.length, globalThis.__probe.revoked.length]
   ```

**Expected:** the blob URL created for a worker is revoked once that worker has loaded.

**Actual:** 3 blob URLs created per profiling session, 0 revoked. Repeat step 4 and it adds 3 more every time, with no bound.

## What I measured

Two long tasks per arm, isolated profile, no extensions:

| Version | `rendererProfiling` | blobs created | revoked | size each |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.129.0-insider | `true` | 6 | **0** | 1,109,433 B |
| 1.129.0-insider | `false` | 0 | 0 | |
| 1.135.0-insider | `true` | 6 | **0** | 1,197,782 B |
| 1.135.0-insider | `false` | 0 | 0 | |

Reading the blob contents back confirms they are worker bootstraps. Each one begins `/*CpuProfileAnalysisWorker*/globalThis._VSCODE_NLS_MESSAGES = [...`.

Console output for the `true` arms:

```
[perf] Render performance baseline is 12ms
[perf] Renderer reported VERY LONG TASK (3000ms), starting profiling session '5a9e25d1-...'
[perf] Renderer reported VERY LONG TASK (3000ms), starting profiling session 'da7a0a87-...'
```

Three blobs per session lines up with the retry loop in `rendererAutoProfiler`, which calls `analyseBottomUp` up to three times and builds a fresh worker each time.

## Cause

In `src/vs/platform/webWorker/browser/webWorkerServiceImpl.ts`, at `08a1ad01b35e41b7412e2290c010cda68bdf6333`.

`getWorkerBootstrapUrl` returns a fresh blob URL (line 117):

```ts
	]).join('')], { type: 'application/javascript' });
	return URL.createObjectURL(blob);
```

`_createWorker` puts it in a local that goes out of scope right away (lines 36-38):

```ts
	const workerUrlWithNls = getWorkerBootstrapUrl(descriptor.label, workerRunnerUrl, this._getWorkerLoadingFailedErrorMessage(descriptor));
	const worker = new Worker(ttPolicy ? ttPolicy.createScriptURL(workerUrlWithNls) as unknown as string : workerUrlWithNls, { name: descriptor.label, type: 'module' });
	return whenESMWorkerReady(worker);
```

The URL is never stored anywhere, so `WebWorker`'s dispose (line 164) has nothing to revoke:

```ts
	this._register(toDisposable(() => {
		this.worker?.then(w => {
			w.onmessage = null;
			w.onmessageerror = null;
			w.removeEventListener('error', errorHandler);
			w.terminate();
		});
		this.worker = null;
	}));
```

`revokeObjectURL` does not appear anywhere in that file.

The correct pattern with the same API is already in the repo. `perfBaseline` in `src/vs/workbench/services/timer/browser/timerService.ts` (line 593):

```ts
	const blobUrl = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
	const worker = createBlobWorker(blobUrl, { name: 'perfBaseline' });
	return new Promise<number>(resolve => {
		worker.onmessage = e => resolve(e.data.value);
	}).finally(() => {
		worker.terminate();
		URL.revokeObjectURL(blobUrl);
	});
```

#253663 fixed the related problem of these workers not being terminated, but it did not touch the blob URL.

## Suggestion

`whenESMWorkerReady` already resolves after the bootstrap has finished importing the real worker script, and that is the point where the blob URL stops being needed. It rejects through `worker.onerror`, so `.finally` covers the load-failure path too:

```ts
	const worker = new Worker(ttPolicy ? ttPolicy.createScriptURL(workerUrlWithNls) as unknown as string : workerUrlWithNls, { name: descriptor.label, type: 'module' });
	return whenESMWorkerReady(worker).finally(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(workerUrlWithNls));
```

I avoided the more common `new Worker(url); URL.revokeObjectURL(url);` idiom on purpose. That one depends on when the worker script fetch resolves the URL, and it has a history of cross-browser inconsistency. Using the ready hook that is already there needs no such assumption.

There is a second thing, independent of the leak. The bootstrap serialises the full NLS table into a 1.1 MB string on every worker creation. That content is deterministic for a given label and script URL, so caching one blob URL per bootstrap would make it bounded. Let me know if that is worth its own issue.

## Why this surfaces as disk usage

Blobs stay in memory until the renderer is under memory pressure, and Chromium then pages them into `blob_storage`. On a 16 GB machine with a lot of windows open they all end up on disk. The on-disk files pack four bootstraps each (I checked the offsets), so 3,203 files corresponded to roughly 12,800 retained blobs.

In #249343 the reporter was asked whether they had turned this setting on deliberately. In my case the answer is no: it came from `experiment: { mode: "startup" }`, and the first I knew about it was the 13 GB.

   ```json
     "method": "listSessions",
     "params": {
       "channel": "ahp-root://",
       "limit": 2
     }
   }
   ```

## Actual

The entire command fails:

```text
-32603 ProviderCatalogUnavailableError:
Provider claude cannot enumerate its native session catalog yet
```

Waiting and retrying does not repair it. The same failure occurs with both a persistent profile and a completely fresh isolated profile.

Meanwhile, all of the following continue to work:

- AHP 1.0 `initialize`
- `ping`
- protected-resource authentication
- Copilot model discovery
- `resolveSessionConfig`
- direct `createSession`
- direct session/chat subscriptions
- chat turns and completion
- reconnect replay
- session disposal

## Expected

One unavailable provider-native external catalogue should not fail the entire Agent Host session catalogue.

Any of these would be preferable:

1. Return locally registered sessions while omitting the unavailable provider's external sessions.
2. Return a partial result with provider-level diagnostics.
3. Mark Claude catalogue discovery unavailable and retry it independently.

## Source-level cause

In `AgentService._migrateLegacyProviderChats`, an undefined provider catalogue throws `ProviderCatalogUnavailableError`. `listSessions()` awaits initial provider migration before listing the Agent Host registry, so one provider blocks every registered session.

## Related, but not duplicate

- #329619 covers ignored `limit`/`cursor` pagination.
- #331155 covers slow Copilot catalogue migration.

This issue is specifically about one unavailable provider failing the whole `listSessions` command, including locally registered sessions from other healthy providers.

title: Shared prompt/customization migration attention service
body:
## Proposal

Add a shared `ICustomizationMigrationService` for editor chat and the Agents Window.

For the active workspace, the service assesses all customization types that may need migration to the Copilot harness. Third-party harness migration is out of scope.

The assessment is demand-driven and runs when:

- a new chat surface opens in the editor;
- the new-session surface opens in the Agents Window;
- an existing session is opened or restored.

It returns whether attention is needed plus categorized findings, severity, and counts. Severity distinguishes cases that remain supported or can be mapped transparently from cases that may stop working. Consumers use this result to show a consistent **customizations need attention** hint appropriate to the impact.

The assessment may also include a small sample of affected customization names if useful for the chosen UX; names are not included in telemetry.

Emit minimal telemetry from the completed assessment: trigger surface, finding category, severity, and count. Do not build separate discovery telemetry for each customization subsystem.

## Discuss

Where should the attention hint take the user to review and act on the findings?

cc @aeschli @hawkticehurst

title: Suggestion: Test coverage for Copilot chat in floating (auxiliary) windows
body:
# Suggestion: Test coverage for Copilot chat in floating (auxiliary) windows

- **Drafted:** 2026-08-27
- **Type:** Suggestion for `microsoft/vscode` (test coverage / regression prevention)
- **Affected area:** Auxiliary (floating) window rendering of Copilot chat and related editor widgets

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

First, thank you for VS Code — it is a pleasure to use, and floating windows plus Copilot chat are a great combination. This is offered gently as a small suggestion, not a complaint.

Why this matters to us: each of these incidents tends to cost roughly half a day of troubleshooting or hunting for a workaround. VS Code is such a powerful and useful IDE that we simply cannot afford not to use it. Our corporate IT team maintains a baseline version as a safe home to fall back to, but that build usually lags well behind and misses helpful features from the latest release — so staying current matters to us. That is why a little extra test coverage around this area would go a long way toward stability.

Over about two weeks we happened to run into two core issues, both while using Copilot chat in a floating/auxiliary window, and both seemingly from the same underlying cause: DOM nodes created against the **main** window's `document` while the component is rendered inside a **child/auxiliary** window (`auxiliaryWindowService.ts` guards `document.createElement` on aux-window documents, so such a call throws instead of rendering).

Because it surfaced at more than one call site, it might be worth a little more automated coverage for the auxiliary-window path. A few ideas:

- Chat session editor in an auxiliary window — moving a chat session editor into an auxiliary window and checking the pane renders without throwing (the `createDormantHost` / "Move to New Window" case).
- Suggest widget in an auxiliary window — triggering `/` completions in a chat input hosted in an auxiliary window and checking the list renders (the #330736 case).
- DOM-creation guard test — rendering the chat input and its popups against an auxiliary-window `document` and checking no "Not allowed to create elements in child window" error occurs.

Recent related issues: #330736 (fixed in 1.134.0 via #330777), #332955, #332924, #332777, and earlier occurrences of the same class #326645, #327958, #320797 (fixed in 1.125.0).

> This is a draft suggestion for `microsoft/vscode`. It cannot be filed from an Enterprise Managed User (EMU) account; it could be submitted from a personal GitHub account or routed through internal/Microsoft support.
>
> **A note of appreciation:** VS Code is a remarkably capable and polished editor, and the floating-window and Copilot chat features are genuinely useful in daily work. Thank you to the Microsoft engineering team for their continued craftsmanship. The notes below are offered gently, only in the hope of being helpful.

---

The sections below are supporting detail for this repository's records.

## Summary

Over about two weeks we happened to run into two VS Code core issues, both while using Copilot chat in a floating/auxiliary window, and both seemingly from the same underlying cause: code that creates DOM nodes against the **main** window's `document` while the component is rendered inside a **child/auxiliary** window. `auxiliaryWindowService.ts` intentionally guards `document.createElement` on aux-window documents (so `x instanceof HTMLElement` keeps working), so such a call throws instead of rendering.

Because it surfaced at more than one call site, it may be that the auxiliary-window path could benefit from a little more automated coverage. This is just a suggestion, not a critique.

## Background: recent incidents

| Incident | Date | Symptom | Root cause / call site | Upstream tracking |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Suggest widget fails in floating chat window | 2026-08-13 | Typing `/` in the chat input renders no suggestion list | `SuggestWidget` measurement creates its element from the aux-window `document` | [#330736](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/330736) — fixed in 1.134.0 via PR [#330777](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330777) |
| Moving a Copilot chat session to a new window fails | 2026-08-27 | Red "The editor could not be opened due to an unexpected error" screen; chat never renders | Chat/agent session editor (`createDormantHost`) creates DOM elements from the wrong window `document` | [#332955](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332955), [#332924](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332924), [#332777](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332777) |

A couple of related, earlier occurrences of the same error class (different call sites) suggest it recurs from time to time:

- [#326645](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326645) — terminal `@xterm/addon-webgl` in an auxiliary window.
- [#327958](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327958) — terminal in an auxiliary window.
- [#320797](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/320797) — `chatImageUtils` (fixed in 1.125.0).

## The common error

```text
Not allowed to create elements in child window JavaScript context.
Always use the main window so that "xyz instanceof HTMLElement" continues to work.
    at document.createElement (workbench.desktop.main.js)
```

## A gentle suggestion

If it seems worthwhile, some automated coverage for Copilot chat rendered in an auxiliary (floating) window might help catch this pattern early. A few ideas:

1. **Chat session editor in an auxiliary window** — moving a chat session editor into an auxiliary window and checking the pane renders without throwing (the `createDormantHost` / "Move to New Window" case).
2. **Suggest widget in an auxiliary window** — triggering `/` completions in a chat input hosted in an auxiliary window and checking the list renders (the #330736 case).
3. **DOM-creation guard test** — rendering the chat input and its popups against an auxiliary-window `document` and checking no "Not allowed to create elements in child window" error occurs.

## Notes

- Analyzed with the assistance of VS Code Copilot. Encountered in a corporate work environment; would be reported from a personal GitHub account.

title: Context-size configuration is lost for extension-provided models in Agent Host
body:
Hi! I’m working on a `LanguageModelChatProvider` for Vercel AI Gateway, and I ran into what looks like an Agent Host projection gap.

I first noticed this through the product: the Vercel models work in both normal Chat and a Local Agent Host session, but the Context Size dropdown only appears in normal Chat.

The provider already includes `contextSize` choices in the model's `configurationSchema`. Normal Chat renders those choices and passes the selection back to the provider. When the same model is used through Agent Host, the model still appears and works, but that configuration is no longer available.

## Reproduction

1. Install an extension that contributes a language model with `configurationSchema.properties.contextSize`.
2. Select the model in normal Chat and confirm that Context Size is available.
3. Start a Local session from the Agents view.
4. Select the same model and open its configuration.

The Context Size control is missing in the Agent Host session.

I think this is adjacent to #328336 and #320824. #329892 is also close, although I’m not sure it’s exactly the same question: that issue is about declaring context-size choices in `chatLanguageModels.json`, while in this case the extension provider has already declared them and normal Chat can render them.

Looking through the current path, it seems like Agent Host reconstructs the reasoning-effort configuration explicitly, but doesn't carry the provider's context-size choices—or its configuration schema more generally. I may be missing a supported hook here.

What is the intended boundary? Should Agent Host preserve the model configuration supplied by an extension provider, or should context size become another explicit capability carried through the bridge?

If there’s already a supported way for a provider extension to make this configuration available in Agent Host, I’d be happy to use it.

title: fix: make ahead-of-time terminal executable resolution best-effort (fixes #333012)
body:
### Summary On a remote (SSH) terminal, `TerminalInstance` eagerly resolves the shell executable ahead of process creation as an optimization. This path calls `TerminalProcessManager.getBackendOS()`, which throws `Failed to get remote environment for remote authority "..."` when the remote agent environment cannot be fetched yet (connection still establishing or dropped). Because the call runs inside the non-disposed `_xtermReadyPromise.then()` chain, the rejection escapes as unhandled-error telemetry even though the OS/executable is re-resolved later through the normal process-creation path. Affects ~117 users across two sibling buckets on Windows and Mac. Fixes microsoft/vscode\#333012 Recommended reviewer: `@meganrogge` ### Culprit Commit No single culprit commit could be pinned. The throw at `terminalProcessManager.ts:594` and the eager-resolution consumer at `terminalInstance.ts` both predate the regression window: `git blame` attributes the `getBackendOS` throw to `f7b171120126` (Megan Rogge, 2022-01-25). The regression-scan comment notes the bucket ID drifts across insider builds throughout the 1.134→1.135 window with no clean first-bad commit, indicating a **pre-existing** latent bug surfacing more frequently (likely a re-bucketing / environmental shift in remote-connection timing) rather than a code regression. Per the pre-existing classification, no culprit is named. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Xterm as _xtermReadyPromise.then participant Instance as TerminalInstance participant PM as TerminalProcessManager participant Remote as RemoteAgentService Xterm->>Instance: eager executable resolution (optimization) Instance->>PM: getBackendOS() PM->>Remote: getEnvironment() Note over Remote: ⚠️ Root cause:
returns null when SSH
remote env unavailable Remote-->>PM: null Note over PM: 💥 throw Error:
Failed to get remote environment PM-->>Instance: rejected promise Note over Instance: instance not disposed →
escapes as unhandled telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts` | crash site | L594 (from stack): `throw new Error("Failed to get remote environment for remote authority ...")` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts` | root cause (consumer) | L557-L558: eager optimization awaits `getBackendOS()`, which throws when the remote env is not yet available, inside the non-disposed `.then()` chain | ### Repro Steps 1. Open a workspace connected to an SSH remote (`ssh-remote+`). 2. Enable terminal shell integration (default) and ensure the shell launch config has no explicit executable. 3. Create a terminal while the remote connection is unavailable or still being established (e.g. the SSH host is briefly unreachable). 4. `getBackendOS()` rejects because `getEnvironment()` returns null; the rejection escapes the eager-resolution path and is reported to error telemetry. Because it depends on remote-connection timing it is non-deterministic; interrupting/degrading the SSH connection during terminal creation increases the likelihood. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts`: the ahead-of-time executable resolution is purely an optimization; the same OS/executable resolution happens again through the normal path in `_createProcess()` → `createProcess()`. The eager block is now wrapped so that if `getBackendOS()` (or the profile resolution) rejects, `os` is reset to `undefined` and a `logService.trace` note is recorded, letting terminal creation continue normally instead of surfacing an unhandled error. This is a consumer-side fix at the optimization site — the producer's deliberate throw (which still feeds telemetry for genuinely required remote-env fetches) is left intact, and no `logService.error` call is removed. The fix targets the code that invokes a throwing call opportunistically, not the crash site itself. **Why this fix works**: after this change, the eager-resolution branch at `terminalInstance.ts:557` can no longer let a `getBackendOS()` rejection escape into the non-disposed `.then()` chain, because the awaited calls are contained and a failure downgrades the optimization to a no-op that the later `_createProcess()` path recovers from. **Alternatives considered**: adding a guard at `getBackendOS()` to return `OS` instead of throwing was rejected — it would silence a legitimate error for callers that genuinely require the remote OS and remove diagnostic signal from the telemetry pipeline. title: Missing loading indicator when streaming output is condensed
body:
## Description

At times where the streaming output is more condensed, there's no visible affordance to know whether the agent is still working. The only way to tell is by checking whether the stop button is showing.

The progress shimmer around the input area should still be running during these condensed streaming states, but it appears to not be showing up.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c516111c-15d5-4ad2-9ccf-302131cdcb2b)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Start an agent session where the streaming output is condensed (few visible tokens/updates).
2. Observe that there is no loading indicator (e.g. shimmer around the input area) shown.
3. The only working-state indicator is the presence of the stop button.

## Expected behavior
The progress shimmer around the input area should continue to indicate that the agent is actively working, even when streaming output is condensed.

## Actual behavior
No loading indicator is shown in this state, making it unclear whether the agent is still working.

---

Reported by Jessie Houghton, flagged by Joanna Oikawa in Slack.

_Created from a [Slack conversation](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C09E1AKMB1P/p1787857687747589?thread_ts=1787857687.747589&cid=C09E1AKMB1P)._

title: Git: Clone destination folder dialog never appears for a repo with no prior clone history
body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🔎 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔍 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No (occurs with "GitHub Pull Requests" extension enabled; not tested with all extensions disabled)

<!-- 🔨 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
>
- VS Code Version: Stable, reproduced on 1.115.0, 1.116.0, 1.134.0, and 1.135.0
- OS Version: Windows 11 (10.0.26200)

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open VS Code with no folder open (File → Close Folder).
2. Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P).
3. Type and run Git: Clone.
4. Either paste a repository URL directly, or select "Clone from GitHub" and pick a repo from the list — a repo that has NEVER been cloned locally before (no prior clone history/metadata for it).
5. After selecting/confirming the repo, the flow skips straight to "Would you like to open the repository?" without ever showing the native folder picker.

Expected Behavior

The native OS folder picker should appear so the destination/parent folder can be chosen before cloning.

Actual Behavior

The destination folder selection step is completely skipped. The Git output channel shows no `git clone` command was ever run — only repeated `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` failures (`fatal: not a git repository`). No folder is created on disk.

Additional Information

- This appears related to #307824 / PR #309247, but that fix's title ("always show clone destination picker when cached repo exists") suggests it only covers repos with existing cached clone metadata.
- Repos that DO have prior clone history (previously cloned, then deleted, tried again via "Clone again") correctly show "Open Existing Repository Clone" and, if reselecting via "Clone again", correctly show the folder picker.
- Repos with NO prior history never show the folder picker, regardless of clone method (URL paste or GitHub picker), across all versions tested (1.115–1.135).

title: Integrated Browser inspect overlay ignores sendElementsToChat.enabled
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: current `main` (also 1.112+ Integrated Browser)
- OS Version: macOS

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `chat.sendElementsToChat.enabled` to `false` (and/or `workbench.browser.enableChatTools` to `false`).
2. Open any page in the Integrated Browser.
3. Right-click a text field or other element (for example to copy/paste).

## Expected

A normal page context menu. No inspect highlight. No Add Element to Chat / Add Comment items.

## Actual

A blue inspect overlay appears (`textarea.classes 500 × 176` chip) and the context menu always includes **Add Element to Chat** and **Add Comment...**.

`chat.sendElementsToChat.enabled` is no longer registered. `workbench.browser.enableChatTools` only gates agent tools. The overlay is painted here on every right-click:

```ts
// src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserViewMainService.ts
if (inspectTarget) {
  // Add Element to Chat / Add Comment...
  void inspectTarget.highlight().catch(() => { });
}
```

`inspectTarget` is only skipped when `aiFeaturesDisabled` (Chat completely off), not when the user disabled element-to-chat.

## Proposed fix

Add `workbench.browser.sendElementsToChat.enabled` (default `true`, migrate from `chat.sendElementsToChat.enabled`) and:

- skip `inspectTarget` / `highlight()` when it is `false`
- gate the Add to Chat toolbar split button and element-selection actions on the same setting

I have this change on a local branch against `main` if useful.

title: Integrated Browser underlines misspellings but offers no way to fix them
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.135.0
- OS Version: macOS

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a page with an editable field in the Integrated Browser.
2. Type a misspelled word (red squiggle appears).
3. Right-click the word.

## Expected

Chrome-style spelling suggestions and **Add to Dictionary**, then the usual edit items.

## Actual

The custom context menu only has Cut / Copy / Paste / Paste and Match Style / Select All / Inspect. Chromium still spellchecks (the underline works), but the replacement menu was never wired up.

`showContextMenu` in `browserViewMainService.ts` builds a replacement menu and never reads `params.misspelledWord` / `params.dictionarySuggestions`.

## Proposed fix

When `params.misspelledWord` is set, prepend Electron's suggestions via `webContents.replaceMisspelling` and **Add to Dictionary** via `session.addWordToSpellCheckerDictionary`.

title: GitHub Copilot inline suggestions fail when parent directory name contains a space on Windows
body:
# GitHub Copilot inline suggestions fail when parent directory name contains a space on Windows

## Description

GitHub Copilot ghost-text/inline completions stop working when the active file is inside a directory whose name contains a space.

The issue is reproducible with a minimal Python file in a clean directory.

Removing the space from the directory name immediately restores inline suggestions.

## Steps to reproduce

Create these two directories:

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\
├── TEST\
│   └── test.py
│
└── TEST TEST\
    └── test.py
```

Both `test.py` files contain exactly:

```python
# calculate the factorial of a number
```

Open `D:\copilot-space-test` in VS Code.

### Test 1 — directory without a space

Open:

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py
```

Press Enter after the comment and start typing:

```python
def 
```

Copilot provides an inline/ghost-text completion as expected.

### Test 2 — directory containing a space

Open the identical file:

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST\test.py
```

Press Enter after the comment and type:

```python
def 
```

No inline suggestion is provided.

The Copilot status menu reports:

```text
No inline suggestion available
```

### Test 3 — rename the directory

Rename:

```text
TEST TEST
```

to something without a space, for example:

```text
TEST-TEST
```

Open the same `test.py` again.

Inline suggestions immediately start working.

## Reproduction commands

The test environment can be created in PowerShell with:

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST" | Out-Null
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST" | Out-Null

'# calculate the factorial of a number' | Set-Content "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py"
Copy-Item "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py" "D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST\test.py"

code "D:\copilot-space-test"
```

## Expected behavior

Copilot inline suggestions should work in both directories.

## Actual behavior

```text
D:\copilot-space-test\TEST\test.py
→ inline suggestions work

D:\copilot-space-test\TEST TEST\test.py
→ no inline suggestions
```

The only relevant difference is the space in the parent directory name.

## Additional information

- The issue is not specific to Python. I originally encountered it with `.tex` files as well.
- It occurs in a clean test directory outside OneDrive.
- I have reproduced it with multiple directory names containing spaces.
- Copilot Chat and Next Edit Suggestions continue to work.
- This appears to be a regression: inline suggestions previously worked in my existing directories containing spaces.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.135.0
- OS: Windows 11 x64 (`Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200`)
- GitHub Copilot: Pro

title: Feedback on new workspace picker (August 27, 2026)
body:
Feedback on the workspace picker changes in #332825.

1. **Differentiate selected/filled pills from recommended/optional pills**
   There should be a clear styling difference between pills that are selected/filled and those that are recommended/optional.

2. **Focused border only appears on the corners**
   The focus border should render continuously around the focused control rather than only at its corners.

3. **Reconsider the harness placement**
   Since the harness is no longer changeable during a session, is it appropriate to move it into the input box? Does this change hide the harness too much?

4. **Add spacing between the icon and agent name**
   Padding is missing between the icon and the agent name.

5. **Folder selection opens the wrong Quick Pick**
   Selecting a folder from either the `...` option or an existing selected option appears to open the wrong Quick Pick menu. The folder-selection Quick Pick should open instead.

6. **Match the surrounding font size**
   The font size should match the rest of the input/new-session area (11px).

7. **Consider descriptive tooltips**
   Should each option have a tooltip that briefly describes what it does?

8. Should we leave room to show an 'x' on hover so folks can dismiss?

title: Agent unexpectedly creates automation for PR monitoring
body:
When asked to monitor a pull request and keep it green, the agent created a scheduled automation without confirming that this was intended.

Expected: treat monitoring as active work in the current session (for example, wait for checks and poll for updates), unless the user explicitly asks for recurring or scheduled automation.

Actual: a persistent hourly automation was created. This was surprising and provided a worse follow-up experience than active in-session monitoring.

title: F3 opens generic tree search in Chat panel and Chat editor
body:
## Description

The chat transcript is backed by a workbench tree, so the generic tree-search keybinding leaks into both the Chat panel and Chat editor. Chat also only binds `F3` and `Shift+F3` while its transcript Find widget is visible, unlike editor Find, which reopens when navigating after it has been hidden.

## Steps to reproduce

### Generic tree search

1. Open the Chat panel or a Chat editor.
2. Focus the chat transcript.
3. Press `F3`.

**Actual:** `F3` invokes `list.find` and opens the generic tree-search widget over transcript rows.

### Hidden transcript Find

1. Open the Chat panel or a Chat editor containing text with multiple matches.
2. Press `Ctrl+F`, enter a query, and navigate to a result.
3. Press `Escape` to hide transcript Find.
4. Focus the transcript and press `F3` or `Shift+F3`.

**Actual:** Transcript Find does not reopen or continue navigating the existing query.

## Expected behavior

- Chat transcripts do not enable the generic tree-search widget.
- `F3` invokes **Find Next in Chat** and `Shift+F3` invokes **Find Previous in Chat** in both the Chat panel and Chat editor.
- If transcript Find is hidden, these commands reopen it without moving focus into its input and continue from the preserved query and active result.
- Embedded editors in chat retain their normal editor Find keybindings.

title: Ctrl+N replaces the existing Chat Editor session instead of opening a new editor
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Open an existing chat session as a Chat Editor.
2. Focus the chat editor.
3. Press Ctrl+N.

### Actual behavior

The existing editor is cleared and replaced with a blank new chat. The old session is no longer open as an editor.

### Expected behavior

The existing session editor remains open, and Ctrl+N opens a separate new Chat Editor.

### Technical details

Both `workbench.action.chat.newChat` and `workbench.action.openChat` are bound to Ctrl+N in a chat editor. The former has the higher keybinding weight and only checks `inChat`, so it wins and clears the current widget even when `inChatEditor` is true. The clear-current-chat binding should not apply inside a Chat Editor, allowing the New Chat Editor action to handle Ctrl+N.

title: Integrated Browser: Chrome DevTools remote-debugging frontend fails with `(blocked:origin)` / "Unsafe attempt to load URL ... from frame with URL chrome-error://chromewebdata/" when not using Remote-SSH/WSL port forwarding
body: Type: Bug Integrated Browser: Chrome DevTools remote-debugging frontend fails with `(blocked:origin)` / "Unsafe attempt to load URL ... from frame with URL chrome-error://chromewebdata/" when not using Remote-SSH/WSL port forwarding ## Description When connecting the Integrated Browser to a remote Chromium DevTools instance (e.g. `QTWEBENGINE_REMOTE_DEBUGGING`, or any `--remote-debugging-port` target) tunneled to `127.0.0.1:` via a plain SSH port forward, navigating to the public DevTools frontend URL (`https://chrome-devtools-frontend.appspot.com/.../inspector.html?ws=127.0.0.1:/devtools/page/`) fails. The integrated-borwser-DevTools network panel shows the `inspector.html` request itself with status `(blocked:origin)`, and the console reports: ``` Unsafe attempt to load URL https://chrome-devtools-frontend.appspot.com/serve_rev/@/inspector.html?ws=127.0.0.1:/devtools/page/ from frame with URL chrome-error://chromewebdata/. Domains, protocols and ports must match. ``` This is caused by Chromium's Private Network Access (PNA) policy: `chrome-devtools-frontend.appspot.com` is a public HTTPS origin, and PNA blocks a public origin from silently reaching a private/loopback address (`127.0.0.1:`) unless the target answers the CORS preflight with `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true` - which a raw `--remote-debugging-port` listener never does. **Interesting behavior:** the exact same flow (same DevTools frontend URL, same forwarded port) works fine in the Integrated Browser when the workspace is opened via **Remote-SSH** or **Remote-WSL** with VS Code's own automatic port forwarding. It only fails when the port is reachable via a manually created SSH tunnel (`ssh -L :localhost: ...`) in a local (non-remote) window. This suggests VS Code's built-in port-forwarding proxy adds headers/behavior that satisfies the PNA preflight, while a plain forwarded TCP socket does not. Confirmed working: opening the identical `127.0.0.1:` URL in a standalone desktop Chrome window works without any issue, in both local and remote setups - the problem is specific to the Integrated Browser's embedded webview. ## Steps to reproduce Error case: 1. Start a process with Chromium remote debugging enabled, e.g. `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, on a remote host. 2. From a local (non-Remote-SSH, non-Remote-WSL) VS Code window, manually forward the port with a plain SSH tunnel: `ssh -L 9222:localhost:9222 user@remotehost -N`. 3. `curl http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list` to confirm the tunnel works and get a `devtoolsFrontendUrl`. 4. Open that `devtoolsFrontendUrl` in the Integrated Browser (`Simple Browser: Show` / `View: Open Integrated Browser`). Success case: 1. Open a remote workspace (ssh/WSL) 2. Start a process with Chromium remote debugging enabled, e.g. `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, on the remote host. 3. From the remote VS Code window, manually forward the port with a plain SSH tunnel: `ssh -L 9222:localhost:9222 user@remotehost -N`. 4. `curl http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list` to confirm the tunnel works and get a `devtoolsFrontendUrl`. 5. Open that `devtoolsFrontendUrl` in the Integrated Browser (`Simple Browser: Show` / `View: Open Integrated Browser`). ## Expected The DevTools frontend loads and connects, as it does when the identical URL is opened in a standalone desktop browser, or in the Integrated Browser under Remote-SSH/Remote-WSL. ## Environment VS Code version: Code 1.135.0 (08d4889f9ec4a1685d257b9b95de036c8e1ce1e5, 2026-08-25T14:26:52Z) OS: Ubuntu 24.04

title: Copilot Chat: custom agents vanish from the dropdown after "renderer closed the MessagePort" (InstantiationService has been disposed)
body: Type: Bug - VS Code Insiders: 1.136.0-insider (commit b7f76c1a31) - OS: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 - Extension: `github.copilot-chat` 0.35.2025120504 - Single profile (`__default__profile__`), user-level agents in `~/.copilot/agents` ### Summary After an extension host is torn down with **`renderer closed the MessagePort`**, the Copilot Chat extension keeps handling an in-flight agent request and throws `InstantiationService has been disposed`. In that window the custom agents dropdown then only offers the built-in `Agent` — other windows in the same session, with their own extension hosts, keep working normally. `Developer: Reload Window` restores it. This looks related to #320759 and #317276, but those reports do not include the disposal trace, so filing the log evidence separately. ### Log evidence `~/AppData/Roaming/Code - Insiders/logs/20260828T064146/window1/exthost/exthost.log`: ``` 2026-08-28 12:03:10.601 [info] Extension host terminating: renderer closed the MessagePort 2026-08-28 12:03:10.675 [error] Error: InstantiationService has been disposed at t._throwIfDisposed (…/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:29:574) at t.createInstance (…/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:29:1228) at m_.getChatEndpoint (…/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:6729:16599) at RQ.getResult (…/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:2823:9223) at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5) at async Mk._requestHandler (…/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:6725:1838) at async r.$invokeAgent (…/vs/workbench/api/node/extensionHostProcess.js) 2026-08-28 12:03:10.678 [error] Error: InstantiationService has been disposed (identical stack) ``` Immediately **before** the termination, the TypeScript language feature's server process exits in the same window: ``` at ChildProcess. (…/extensions/typescript-language-features/dist/extension.js) at ChildProcess.emit (node:events:509:28) at emit (node:internal/child_process:972:14) 2026-08-28 12:03:10.601 [info] Extension host terminating: renderer closed the MessagePort ``` Possibly coincidental, but the ordering was consistent in the one occurrence captured. ### This is not a normal shutdown I checked every `exthost.log` from the last six days to rule out ordinary window closes: | Termination reason | Count | `disposed` errors | |---|---|---| | `received terminate message from renderer` (normal) | 25 | 0 | | **`renderer closed the MessagePort`** | **1** | **2** | Only the abnormal MessagePort closure produces the error, so the correlation is clean rather than incidental noise. ### Steps to reproduce Not deterministic. Conditions when observed: 1. Many windows open concurrently (26 `Code - Insiders.exe` processes), several with large TypeScript monorepos. 2. Chat is mid-request when the renderer drops the MessagePort. 3. That window's agents dropdown afterwards shows only `Agent`; user-level agents from `~/.copilot/agents` are gone. 4. Other windows are unaffected. 5. `Developer: Reload Window` fixes the affected window. ### Expected Either the extension host tears down without a pending `$invokeAgent` reaching a disposed `InstantiationService`, or the request is cancelled cleanly and agent discovery re-initialises when the window recovers — rather than the window being left with no custom agents until a manual reload. ### Ruled out - Profile mismatch — all 47 workspaces map to `__default__profile__`. - Workspace-level overrides — no `.github/agents` or `.claude/agents`, no chat settings in `.vscode/settings.json`. - Malformed agent files — all 9 have valid frontmatter, a `name`, no BOM, no duplicate names. - Extension version skew — a single `copilot-chat` version installed.

title: Allow disabling Copilot harness built-in tools in Chat: Open Customizations
body:
Allow users to enable or disable individual Copilot harness built-in tools from: **Chat: Open Customizations → Tools → Copilot** ## Current behavior When the **Copilot** harness is selected, the Tools page displays the tools built into the Copilot runtime, but they are read-only. Users can enable or disable client-side and extension-provided tools, but cannot disable Copilot built-in tools such as `task`. The built-in tools also do not appear in **Chat: Manage Tool Approval**, so users cannot require confirmation before they are invoked. For example, the `task` tool can delegate work to a sub-agent. That sub-agent can use a different model and reasoning effort from those selected for the parent conversation. It may therefore change the expected review behavior, latency, and model usage without explicit user confirmation. I've also tryed adding the following setting but it also cannot be used because `task` is not recognized as an approval-configurable VS Code tool: ```json "chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval": { "task": false } ``` ## Requested behavior In **Chat: Open Customizations → Tools → Copilot**, allow users to toggle individual Copilot built-in tools in the same way that client-side tools can be toggled. When a built-in tool is disabled: - It should not be advertised to the model. - The model should not be able to invoke it. - The selection should persist at the user-profile level, consistently with the existing Tools customization UI. For example, disabling `task` should ensure that work is performed by the model and reasoning effort selected for the parent conversation rather than being delegated to a separately configured sub-agent. It would also be useful for Copilot built-in tools to appear in **Chat: Manage Tool Approval**, so users could choose between: 1. Enabled without confirmation. 2. Enabled but always requiring confirmation. 3. Disabled entirely. The primary request is the ability to disable these tools from the existing **Chat: Open Customizations → Tools** interface. ## Motivation Tool selection affects more than filesystem permissions. Built-in tools can influence: - Which model performs the work. - Reasoning effort and review quality. - Premium request or model usage. - Latency. - Whether work is delegated to another context. - Reproducibility of agent behavior. Users should be able to control these capabilities explicitly, especially when the UI already presents built-in tools alongside configurable client-side tools. Natural-language instructions such as “do not use sub-agents” are not an enforceable substitute for disabling the tool. ## Related issues - #323371 documents that Copilot CLI built-in tools are intentionally displayed as read-only. - #300411 requests model and tool parameters for `runSubagent`. - #309540 requests user approval for more expensive sub-agent models. - #333026 reports problems toggling tools in Manage Tool Approval, but Copilot built-in tools are not shown there in this case.
